what_it_is: A ChainSpot-side experiment (not pyto) that is the fourth checkpoint in a series (S0→S1→S2→S3) proving a "Python quick_anno" authoring/investigation pattern: a tiny first-class Python PxC/PCR/PQL core (`packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/`) that consumes a real production TS Stage's exported snapshot, re-seeds it as Python Parts, runs one bounded Python PCR Calculation, queries the result with PQL, emits Mermaid, and materializes a "neon-first" correctness sheet — applied here to S3's visible-Tee detection. Commit message: "quick_anno: materialize S3 visible tee investigation" (19b9b92, git log -1 --format=%B). The checkpoint explicitly does NOT accept S3 as correct: 3 of 18 production-accepted Tee objects turned out to be iOS map-chrome false positives (S3_VALIDATION.md).
commit_message: quick_anno: materialize S3 visible tee investigation
addressing: Addresses are bare dotted strings, not a tree with an explicit root/mount mechanism. `Part` is defined as "A semantic PxC address. Identity is the address, not the current value." (19b9b92:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/core.py:13). `Calculation` enforces one prefix rule only: "Calculation address must start with 'fn.'" (19b9b92:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/core.py:33-34); Part addresses carry no equivalent enforced rule at all — any string passes `Part.__post_init__` as long as it's non-empty (core.py:17-19). In practice this tip uses three observed prefix families by convention only, never validated in code: `px.*` for durable stage-produced state (`px.tees.rings.candidates`, `px.tees.family.measured`, `px.tees.family`, `px.tees`, `px.tees.px` in s3.py:33-37; `px.badges.objects`, `px.badges.px`, `px.badges.muted` in s1.py:33-35), `scratch.*` for PCR-derived investigation output (`scratch.s3.rejectedCandidates`, `scratch.s3.visibleTeeSummary` in s3.py:38-39; `scratch.s1.ownershipSummary` in s1.py:35), and `fn.*` for Calculation identity (`fn.quickAnno.s3.summarizeVisibleTees` in s3.py:56). PQL treats prefix matching as first-class: "Exact Parts and address prefixes are first-class; refinement stays ordinary Python." (19b9b92:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/pql.py:20), implemented as `PQL.prefix(prefix)` doing `address.startswith(prefix)` over `pxc.items()` (pql.py:37-47) — i.e. mounts/scoping exist only as a runtime string-prefix query, not as a declared address-space structure. There is no `namespace`, `mount`, or `root` concept anywhere in this surface (grep across experiments/quick-anno-python and packages/quick_anno_py returns zero hits for "namespace" or "mount"; the only "root" hits are the filesystem repo root, e.g. s1.py:8 `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`). Nothing in this tip states or implements the owner's "connection" principle — no discussion of what a root segment should discriminate, no rule against a generic label, and no explicit statement that addresses connect across Stages/LABs by design (the connection is implicit only in that S1's `px.badges.*` outputs are read by S2, and S2's outputs feed S3, purely through the shared production PxC object passed stage to stage — `s2.pxc` into `s3Contract.execute` in export_s3_snapshot.cjs:29-31 — never through the quick_anno-Python address space itself, which starts fresh per stage from a JSON snapshot).
viewer_and_pcr_render: The `PrincipleComponentRender` shape from origin.md is directly instantiated as literal JSON keys in `graph.py`'s authoring-only `Pcr.to_pcr_dict()`: `return {"PrincipleComponentRender": self.name, "Ticks": ticks}` (19b9b92:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/graph.py:111), each Tick holding `{"name": tick, "Calculations": calculations}` (graph.py:110) — this matches origin.md's `PrincipleComponentRender -> Tick[]`, `Tick -> Calculation[]` shape exactly, but `graph.Pcr` is explicitly non-executing: "This deliberately does not execute ChainSpot calculations... Execution remains owned by ChainSpot/PxC." (graph.py:31-33). The executable sibling, `pcr.PCR` (pcr.py), does run and produces `TickTestimony(name, calculations: tuple[CalculationTestimony,...])` per Tick (pcr.py:68-71) and a `PcrRun(pcr, ticks, results)` (pcr.py:74-78) — but there is no receipt object, no `observe` flag, no `result_sha256`, no `shadowed_inputs`, and no digest anywhere in this pcr.py (absent by comparison with pyto's `pcr.py:95-128` cited in tick-observability-ledger.md section 3 — this quick_anno PCR is strictly simpler and keeps full values in `PcrRun.results`, never digesting them: `results[invocation.id] = value` (pcr.py:162) with no digest step). What a person actually sees is not the PCR/testimony JSON but the neon PNG sheet: `materialize_s3_neon.py` composites six fixed panels — ring candidates (cyan), enclosing frames (orange) plus accepted family (green), accepted visible Tee objects (green boxes + magenta center crosses), exact TeePx in "18 readable local-context crops" (magenta halo over dimmed crop, `exact_local_crops`, materialize_s3_neon.py:52-84), the actual remaining raster with TeePx punched transparent over checkerboard (`remaining`, materialize_s3_neon.py:97-107), and rejected/not-accepted categories in red/yellow/orange (`rejected_panel`, materialize_s3_neon.py:110-127) — assembled by `sheet()` into one PNG (materialize_s3_neon.py:144-190). This is fed per-Stage, not per-Tick: the checkpoint doc states the boundary explicitly — "its cost is the highest of any repeatable view" is not said here, but the shape is: one correctness sheet per Stage snapshot (S1, S2, S3 each get their own `generated/DashsTrack-S{n}/` sheet), sourced from a single `snapshot.json` written by the corresponding `export_s{n}_snapshot.cjs`, not from `PcrRun.ticks`/`results` at all — the bounded Python PCR Calculation in this tip (`fn.quickAnno.s3.summarizeVisibleTees`, s3.py:55-67) only ever produces the numeric summary written to `python-summary.json`/`python-rejected.json` (s3.py:90-93) and the Mermaid file (s3.py:94); the neon sheet is built straight from the raw JS-exported snapshot dict by `materialize_s3_neon.py`, entirely independent of the Python PCR/Tick run. There is no dependency-free browser page or "Kibana for Ticks" viewer anywhere in this tip (grep for "viewer"/"storybook" across the surface returns zero hits) — the only rendered surface is these static PNGs.
storage: No backend beyond the filesystem and in-memory Python dicts: `PxC` is `self._values: dict[str, Any]` (core.py:50), no persistence, no serialization method of its own. There is no DuckDB anywhere in this tip (grep across experiments/quick-anno-python and packages/quick_anno_py for "duckdb" returns zero hits) — this is "missing" relative to pyto's materials-store plans, not present in this branch at all. Content addressing is also absent: `PxC.set` classifies a write only as `"replacement"` vs `"new-address"` by whether the address key already exists (core.py:62-66), never by hashing the value — there is no `result_sha256` / digest concept in this pcr.py at all (contrast with pyto's `pcr.py:125` per tick-observability-ledger.md). What is actually persisted is one plain JSON snapshot per Stage per course, written by the Node exporter: `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'snapshot.json'), JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2))` (19b9b92:experiments/quick-anno-python/export_s3_snapshot.cjs:102), tagged with a schema string `schema: 'chainspot-quick-anno-s3-snapshot@1'` (export_s3_snapshot.cjs:60) — versioned-by-string-suffix rather than content-addressed. Rendered panel PNGs are archived by filename convention keyed on Stage+label: `` const file = `${stage}-${slug(panel.label)}.png`; ... panels[`${stage}:${panel.label}`] = file; `` (export_s3_snapshot.cjs:38-40), then re-opened by that same string key in the materializer: `` Image.open(out_dir / snapshot['panels']['s3:CroppedImage']) `` (materialize_s3_neon.py:163). This is filename-as-address, not a store with a facade — directly contradicting the owner's "storage as the precise opposite of S3[the cache system, i.e. Amazon S3]" thesis (ULTRACODE-WEEK.md Reframing 5): here storage is literally flat files named by a slug of a human label, with no declared Part kind, no backend selection, and outputs are explicitly and deliberately NOT checked in: "Generated files land under `experiments/quick-anno-python/generated/` and are deliberately not checked in by this proof." (19b9b92:experiments/quick-anno-python/README.md:29-31, "not checked in" line).
materialization_and_ticks: "Materialize" in this tip means exactly the origin.md verb — turning execution state into a rendered, inspectable artifact — but it operates per-Stage snapshot, not per-Tick. The house rule carried over from pyto/ChessLab lineage is stated as its own convention: "A subtle render is not accepted as the first correctness proof; **neon first** is the investigation convention." (19b9b92:experiments/quick-anno-python/S1_CHECKPOINT.md, "neon first" line) and repeated as a numbered step in the delegation recipe: "7. materialize a **neon-first** visual correctness check; 8. visually inspect the materialization before claiming success;" (S1_CHECKPOINT.md, "Delegate from here" list). Ticks in the executable `pcr.PCR` are real synchronization/observability units — `PcrRun.ticks: tuple[TickTestimony,...]` groups `CalculationTestimony(id, calculation, inputs, args, into)` per Tick (pcr.py:60-78) exactly mirroring pyto's `PcrRun.ticks -> TickTestimony(name, calculations)` shape (tick-observability-ledger.md section 3, item "Already present") — but in this S3 checkpoint there is only one Tick used at all (`"InspectVisibleTeeFamily"`, s3.py:70-80) wrapping a single Calculation, so the multi-Tick observability the ledger flags as missing in pyto (a Tick materializer that emits per-Tick panels) is equally absent here: the neon sheet is built directly from the Node-exported snapshot dict, never from `PcrRun.ticks`/`PcrRun.results`. So this tip demonstrates the PCR/Tick/Calculation object shape working end-to-end for a trivial one-Tick summary, but does not demonstrate or need a Tick-level materializer — the "materializer" that exists (`materialize_s3_neon.py`) is a Stage-snapshot materializer, confirming the ledger's Gap 3/§3 diagnosis (pyto lacks a `materialize_run(run: PcrRun, pxc: PxC)` function) is not answered by this ChainSpot-side work either.
receipts_and_telemetry: Two distinct and non-overlapping receipt shapes appear. (1) Production TS Stage receipts are opaque preformatted text, passed through unmodified: `s0Receipt: s0.receiptText, s1Receipt: s1.receiptText, s2Receipt: s2.receiptText, s3Receipt: s3.receiptText` in the snapshot (19b9b92:experiments/quick-anno-python/export_s3_snapshot.cjs:63-66), also written standalone as `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 's3.receipt.txt'), s3.receiptText + '\n')` (export_s3_snapshot.cjs:103) — these are opaque strings from the JS runtime, never parsed or structured by the Python side. (2) The Python `pcr.PCR.run` produces no receipt object at all — no `Receipt` dataclass exists in `pcr.py`; the closest analogue is `PxWrite(address, kind)` returned by `PxC.set` (core.py:40-43,62-66), which records only an address and a `"new-address"`/`"replacement"` kind, no reads, no digest, no calculation identity, no shadowed-inputs. Telemetry in the sense of a parallel logging/metrics channel is explicitly refused: "No convenience was added to PxC/PQL/PCR... no new parallel telemetry or semantic store was introduced." (19b9b92:experiments/quick-anno-python/S3_VALIDATION.md, final paragraph). So relative to pyto's `Receipt` fields cited in tick-observability-ledger.md section 3 (`declared_consumes`/`actual_consumes`, `writes: PxWrite`, `shadowed_inputs`), this tip's PCR carries only the `into`-write half of that (`PxWrite`) and nothing on the reads side — `CalculationTestimony.inputs: dict[str, str]` records only `"px:<address>"` / `"fn:<calc_id>"` reference tags (pcr.py:149,157), not a declared-vs-actual distinction.
reusable_now: The `PrincipleComponentRender: name, Ticks: [{name, Calculations: [...]}]` JSON shape in `19b9b92:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/graph.py:89-111` is a ready-made literal-key convention pyto could adopt verbatim for a portable PCR export format, since pyto's `pcr.py` (per tick-observability-ledger.md) already has the equivalent internal shape but no serializer producing these exact keys.

The 'neon-first' correctness-sheet convention and its concrete panel vocabulary (owned/muted-added/removed as color-coded overlays, exact-pixel local-context crops instead of isolated masks, remaining-raster-as-checkerboard) in `19b9b92:experiments/quick-anno-python/materialize_s3_neon.py:18-190` is directly portable to pyto's neon.py, which already states the same house rule ("neon first — if a panel needs pixel-peeping to tell whether the computation happened, the materialization failed", per tick-observability-ledger.md §3) but per that ledger has no actual per-Stage/per-Tick materializer wired up yet — this file is a working reference implementation to port function-by-function (draw_boxes, exact_local_crops, checkerboard, remaining, sheet).

The `PxC`/`Part`/`Calculation`/`PCR`/`Tick`/`PQL` core in `19b9b92:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/{core.py,pcr.py,pql.py}` is a minimal, dependency-free, ~300-line reference implementation of the exact same architecture pyto already has (fail-loud store, address-as-identity Part, fn.-prefixed Calculation, Tick grouping, prefix-based PQL) — useful as a smaller worked example / test fixture for pyto's own core, though pyto's is already more complete (has receipts with declared/actual consumes).

The delegate/checkpoint discipline itself — numbered steps in `19b9b92:experiments/quick-anno-python/S1_CHECKPOINT.md` ("Delegate from here", 10 steps: snapshot in, seed Parts, name Calculations, publish scratch Parts, PQL not ad-hoc state, materialize neon-first, visually inspect before claiming success, emit Mermaid/testimony, add convenience only after friction) — is a directly reusable per-Stage transfer checklist/template for pyto's own week-by-week Stage-transfer work.

The explicit 'HUH' failure-reporting convention in `19b9b92:experiments/quick-anno-python/S3_VALIDATION.md` (state expected vs. encountered, name exact pixel coordinates of the false positives, mark PASS/FAIL per axis rather than one verdict) is a reusable format for pyto's own validation docs / {?} entries when a materialization surfaces a real defect rather than a design question.

quick_anno: point the survey summary at the solved bMute section

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Noe2WoCiT3tj3YNJwPp6tM
what_it_is: A ChainSpot-side CV forensics investigation, not a PxC/PCR engine change. The tip is the third of a series (S1→S2→S3) applying "the bounded transfer pattern" (6309ff1:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/investigation.py:1-13) — real production Stage output exported from Node → first-class Python PxC Parts → a small PCR composition → a PQL query → a neon-first correctness sheet — to ChainSpot's S3 visible-Tee detector. `git diff --stat` against `main` shows the whole repo differing (no shared history reachable in this shallow clone: `git merge-base main 6309ff1` fails), so I diffed this commit against its actual parent 5c87d48 (the S2 checkpoint) instead, which isolates the real content: 14 files, +1377/-300 (`git -C /home/user/samuelpmahan/chainspot diff --stat 5c87d48 6309ff1`). This IS the reference material `pyto/research/tick-observability-ledger.md` rows 3–4, 25–26 and section 3 already cite as `pyto/reference/chainspot-quick-anno/*` — same file names, same `chainspot_quick_anno` package (core.py, pcr.py, pql.py, neon.py, investigation.py). It is the precursor of pyto's own core.py/pcr.py/pql.py, one generation earlier: no `observe=True`, no `Receipt`, no digests, no durations — those were added later in pyto's own Day 2.
addressing: No explicit "root"/mount/registration rule is stated in this tip — the {?} root and the owner's "connection" statement post-date it (both are in pyto/questions.md, produced 2026-09-09; this tip is 2026-09-07). What exists is the address CONVENTION pyto later inherited almost verbatim: a hard `fn.` prefix enforced in code for Calculations — `if not self.address.startswith("fn."): raise ValueError("Calculation address must start with 'fn.'")` (6309ff1:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/core.py:33-34) — and two informal, unenforced namespaces used by convention only: `px.*` for Parts seeded from real production material (`Part('px.tees.rings')`, `Part('px.badges.objects')` — 6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/s3.py:28-31, 6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/s1.py:24-26) and `scratch.*` for Python-owned derived/investigation-only Parts (`Part('scratch.s3.ringLedger')`, `Part('scratch.s1.ownershipSummary')` — same lines). Every address segment after the prefix discriminates by Stage and concept (`px.tees.rings` vs `px.tees.family` vs `px.tees.px` vs `px.tees`, `px.badges.objects` vs `px.badges.px` vs `px.badges.muted`) — none of the roots are generic; each PCR is itself named `<Stage>.quick-anno` (`PCR('S3.quick-anno')`, `PCR('S1.quick-anno')`) and each Tick is named for what it does (`'InspectOwnership'`, `'AccountRings'`, `'CheckBalance'`), never a generic label. "No registration" for Parts is literal: `PxC.set` just writes into a plain dict keyed by address string (6309ff1:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/core.py:62-66, `_values: dict[str, Any]`), no schema, no namespace object, no mount step. The one place addresses ARE resolved/rewritten automatically is `PCR.calc`: if a bound Part's address already has a registered writer in this PCR, the binding is silently rewritten from a Part reference to a `ResultRef` to that writer's invocation id — "if isinstance(source, Part) and source.address in self._writers: source = ResultRef(self._writers[source.address])" (6309ff1:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/pcr.py:113-116) — so within one PCR, an address always resolves to its most recent producer rather than a stale store read; this is pyto's identical `{?} SilentRules` mechanism, present here already, unlabelled as a question. Missing in this tip: any statement of why the root should "carry connection" (that's the owner's later, 2026-09-09 framing) and any prefix beyond `px.`/`scratch.`/`fn.` (no `data.users`, no per-user or cross-project addressing — TableScope/CrossProjectReuse do not exist yet here).
viewer_and_pcr_render: There is no Tick-keyed viewer here — confirming tick-observability-ledger row 3's classification ("Neon correctness sheet... keyed by Stage, e.g. `s3:CroppedImage`... not by Tick"). What a person sees is one PNG contact-sheet PER STAGE PER COURSE, `s3-neon-correctness-sheet.png`, built by `sheet(panels)` compositing named `panel()`s top-to-bottom (6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/materialize_s3_neon.py:100-131), fed not from `PcrRun` at all but directly from the raw Node-bridge `snapshot.json` dict (rings/family/tees arrays) plus the canonical raster image — the Python PCR's `results`/testimony are NOT what the sheet renders from; the sheet is a second, independent consumer of the same snapshot the PCR also consumes (6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/s3.py:25-38 vs 6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/materialize_s3_neon.py:44-53). S3 grew the sheet from 9 to 11 panels specifically because full-panel bounding boxes could not answer "what is this object", only "where is it": "panels 1-7 prove where each object was accepted and never what it is. Identity precedes geometry; a full-course panel cannot establish identity at course zoom" (6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/S3_CHECKPOINT.md:110-112), which is why `neon.crops` was added — a contact strip of one upscaled, subject-marked crop per object (6309ff1:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/neon.py:103-116, "Identity precedes geometry: a full-course panel proves where an object was accepted, never what it is. This answers the second question."). Values shown are literal pixels/boxes drawn on the canonical raster, colour-coded per rejection bucket (grey=diamond-dropped, red=Badge-muted, orange=unframed, magenta=voted-out, green=accepted — 6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/materialize_s3_neon.py:100-127); no scalar/JSON Part value is rendered in the sheet. Separately, `PCR.mermaid()` DOES render per-Tick, per-Calculation structure as a picture (subgraph-per-Tick, node-per-invocation, edges labelled by argument name — 6309ff1:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/pcr.py:179-219, near-identical to what tick-observability-ledger row 25 cites in pyto's own pcr.py), but it is explicitly NOT the pattern's spine: "Not part of the pattern's spine: nothing consumes the .mmd, and a two-node graph needs no diagram. The emitter stays because the day a Stage graph has a dozen nodes it will be the cheapest way to see it" (6309ff1:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/investigation.py:91-93), and both call sites leave it commented out (`# inv.write_mermaid(pcr) renders the composition when a graph needs a picture.` — 6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/s3.py:104). So today: the picture a person actually opens (the neon sheet) is Stage-keyed and value-bearing but PCR-blind; the picture that is Tick-keyed and PCR-shaped (Mermaid) is structure-only, value-blind, and unused. Nothing in this tip resembles "PCR is Kibana" as a render-definition abstraction — that framing is pyto's later (2026-09-09) Reframing 4, not present here; each Stage's materializer is a bespoke hand-written script, exactly the row-3/row-30 pattern the ledger critiques ("no shared engine").
storage: No backend, no DuckDB, no sqlite, no content addressing anywhere in this tip (grep for all three across `experiments/quick-anno-python` and `packages/quick_anno_py` returns zero hits). `PxC` is a bare in-process Python dict: `self._values: dict[str, Any] = {}` and `self._calculations: dict[str, Calculation[Any, Any]] = {}` (6309ff1:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/core.py:49-51) — it dies with the process; nothing is retained, replayed, or hashed as a Part identity. The only sha256 in the whole diff verifies the raw corpus INPUT file's bytes against its Git-LFS pointer before running ("Input verified by content, not by filename... sha256 e6616738640eee1d05d8cc2b59dd657f24b4a5a01dc2f68571b7e44c6f372b8a" — 6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/S3_VALIDATION.md:17-23) — an external provenance check, not a PxC key. What IS "archived," and why: every run's Node-bridge-exported `snapshot.json`, the Python-derived `python-summary.json`, the production `s3.receipt.txt`, the Mermaid `.mmd`, and every neon PNG are written as plain files under `experiments/quick-anno-python/generated/<Course>-<Stage>/` (named in 6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/export_s3_snapshot.cjs:138-140 and 6309ff1:experiments/quick-anno-python/S3_VALIDATION.md:129-150) — but `.gitignore` explicitly EXCLUDES that whole `generated/` tree from the repo ("quick_anno Python investigation outputs — regenerated by experiments/quick-anno-python/s<N>.py, never committed" — 6309ff1:.gitignore, added this diff), so nothing here is retained across sessions; it is scratch-disk output for one interactive run, reproduced fresh every time the repro command is rerun. what_it_is:
A checkpoint of the "quick_anno" experiment: a small first-class Python PxC/PCR/Part/Calculation/Tick/PQL core (packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/{core,pcr,pql,graph}.py) plus a driver (experiments/quick-anno-python/s1.py) that shells out to the real TS ChainSpot runtime (export_s1_snapshot.cjs, using the built @chainspot/alg S0/S1 stage contracts) to get a real S1 snapshot for Dash's Track, loads Badge/owned/muted Parts into the Python PxC, runs a tiny Python PCR ("S1.quick-anno") that publishes a derived scratch Part, queries it back with PQL, emits a Mermaid view of the composition, and produces a 7-panel "neon-first" correctness contact sheet with Pillow (materialize_s1_neon.py). It supersedes an earlier, purely-authoring proof (experiments/quick-anno-python/README.md, base b5a6ae0) that only emitted PCR JSON + Mermaid without touching real data. This is exactly the tree the pyto research docs already cite as `pyto/reference/chainspot-quick-anno/*` (tick-observability-ledger.md rows 3-4, 25-28), so the port pyto is currently doing has this ChainSpot commit as its literal source.

Caveat on `git diff --stat main 82f8fc9`: the archive-fetched `82f8fc9` has no recorded parent in this shallow clone (`git show -s --format=%P 82f8fc9` returned empty) and `git merge-base main 82f8fc9` fails — the two tips are unrelated grafted histories in this shallow fetch, not a normal feature-branch diff. The stat (1305 files changed, 158602 insertions/139825 deletions) is effectively a whole-tree comparison against a different, mostly-disjoint snapshot of the same repo, not a scoped PR diff — I read it as confirmation that this is a large, long-lived working tree rather than as a semantic diff, and instead scoped this report to the files under experiments/quick-anno-python/, packages/quick_anno_py/, and the production files they call into.

What the code actually enforces: Part identity is address-only and unconstrained beyond non-empty (core.py:17-19, `"""A semantic PxC address. Identity is the address, not the current value."""` at core.py:13) — any string is a legal Part address, so "px." vs "scratch." vs anything else is pure convention, never checked. Calculation addresses are the one enforced prefix rule: `if not self.address.startswith("fn."): raise ValueError("Calculation address must start with 'fn.'")` (core.py:33-34). The one addressing invariant PCR enforces is single-writer-per-address plus direct-result rewrite, not a naming rule: `prior = self._writers.get(output.address); if prior is not None: raise ValueError(f"PCR '{self.name}' has multiple writers for '{output.address}'")` (pcr.py:120-122), exercised by test_first_class.py:38-49 and, in the declarative (non-executing) authoring surface, by graph.py:73-74 and test_graph.py:31-36. (graph.py:32-34), echoed in README.md:8: "This is intentionally not a second ChainSpot executor. Python authors a graph; ChainSpot/PxC remains the intended execution owner." Values ARE live in memory (`results: dict[str, Any]` on PcrRun, pcr.py:78, populated at pcr.py:162) but nothing here serializes them — `s1.py:72` writes only the single terminal `scratch.s1.ownershipSummary` value to `python-summary.json`, not `run.results` or any per-Tick file, so per-Tick materialization of intermediate values does not exist in this tip either, matching the exact gap pyto's own ledger names. This is intentionally not a second ChainSpot executor. Python authors a graph; ChainSpot/PxC remains the intended execution owner." The commit's own diff (isolated by grepping the huge main-vs-tip diff --stat for quick-anno/PCR/PQL/PxC paths) is small and self-contained; the remaining ~1290 files in the raw `diff --stat main f3ecab3` (skills, docs/unported/*, .task/* tickets, storybook config, etc.) are unrelated branch-vs-main divergence noise — none of those .task/*.md or docs/*.md files mention PCR/PxC/PQL/quick_anno at all (`grep -l "PCR|PxC|PQL|quick_anno" .task/*.md` returned nothing), so they are excluded from the findings below and noted as noise rather than tip content.
commit_message: quick_anno: test first-class Python PxC PQL PCR behavior
addressing: Root/prefix rule, verbatim: `f3ecab3:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/core.py:33-34` — `Calculation.__post_init__`: `if not self.address.startswith("fn."):  raise ValueError("Calculation address must start with 'fn.'")`. Part addresses carry no such enforced prefix in Python but every example and test uses `px.` (`core.py:11-13`: "A semantic PxC address. Identity is the address, not the current value."; e.g. `f3ecab3:packages/quick_anno_py/tests/test_first_class.py:6-7` `Part("px.badges")`, `Part("px.remaining.afterBadges")`). The TS reference this transfers from enforces the same two-namespace rule structurally, not just by convention: `f3ecab3:packages/alg/src/stages/S0/exp/mermaid-pcr/compiler.ts:31-32` — a Mermaid node "must label fn.* or px.*" or compilation fails (`fail(\`node '${node[1]}' must label fn.* or px.*.\`)`), and `compiler.ts:73` rejects "PxC-to-PxC edges require a Calculation" — i.e. a Part can never address another Part directly; every edge into a Part must pass through a named `fn.` Calculation. This is the closest thing in the tip to an explicit addressing rule, and it is exactly two segments deep (kind prefix, then a dotted semantic path) — there is no root segment beyond the `px`/`fn` kind tag itself, so the tip does not engage the owner's "meaningless root" critique at all; the root here is a bare kind discriminator (`px`/`fn`), not a connective name. No mount, namespace-registration, or per-application addressing concept appears anywhere in the tip: `grep -rn "mount"` across the extracted tip found only 2 unrelated hits (LAB page/pin \"namespaces\" in `scripts/chainspot-lab/README.md:185`, a pre-existing doc unrelated to this commit) and no `mount`/registration logic in any of the new PxC/PCR/PQL files. Alignment between the graph-authoring layer and the executable layer is done by direct-result rewrite, not addressing: once a Part has a writer inside the same graph, any later `**inputs` binding to that Part's address is silently rewritten to a `ValueRef`/`ResultRef` pointing at the producing invocation id — Python: `f3ecab3:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/graph.py:65-68` (\"Match the Mermaid compiler's direct-result behavior: once a Part has a writer in this graph, consuming that Part refers to the writer result\") and `f3ecab3:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/pcr.py:112-116`; TS original: `f3ecab3:packages/alg/src/stages/S0/exp/mermaid-pcr/compiler.ts:92` (`const producer = source.kind === 'fn' ? source.id : writers.get(source.label);`). Serialized bindings carry an explicit `kind` discriminator, `{"kind":"px","ref":...}` vs `{"kind":"fn","ref":...}` (`graph.py:98-102`), and at run time the testimony format is `\"px:<address>\"` vs `\"fn:<calculation_id>\"` strings (`f3ecab3:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/pcr.py:149,157`, verified in `test_first_class.py:35`: `assert add_testimony.inputs == {\"left\": \"fn:double\", \"right\": \"fn:double\"}`). Duplicate-writer and duplicate-id are the only other address-shaped rules enforced: `pcr.py:120-122` (\"PCR ... has multiple writers for ...\"), `graph.py:72-74`, `compiler.ts:77`. Nothing in the tip addresses the owner's \"connection, not a generic label\" root critique directly — there is no discussion of what the root segment should discriminate; the tip's whole addressing surface is the two-letter kind tag plus an unconstrained dotted string.
viewer_and_pcr_render: The tip's Python side has no viewer of its own — it only emits data (`to_pcr_json`, `to_mermaid`) for later rendering (`f3ecab3:experiments/quick-anno-python/README.md:16-19`). The real viewer/PCR-render evidence in this commit lives on the TS/Svelte side it mirrors, and it matches the owner's "PCRs are Kibana" framing precisely: `f3ecab3:packages/alg/src/exec/pcr.ts:17-21` — \"Storybook-facing composition of already-executed Tick testimony. PCR has deliberately no run() method: the production gateway is the only execution authority and hands this function the receipts it already produced.\" `pcr.ts:90` further separates render identity from run identity: \"View identity is a pure projection of a frozen PCR; it cannot execute CV,\" implemented as `pcrRenderId(pcr, viewArgs)` hashing `{runResultId, viewArgs}` — changing `viewArgs` (zoom, materializationView, showGrid, etc.) changes only the render hash, never the underlying `runResultId`. This is asserted directly in the test suite: `f3ecab3:tests/unit/pcr.test.ts:50,63-72` — describe block \"PCR composes testimony without becoming an engine\"; test \"changing View Args changes only render identity\" asserts `pcrRenderId(pcr,{zoom:2}) !== pcrRenderId(pcr,{zoom:4})` while `pcr.runResultId` is unchanged; test at `pcr.test.ts:74-133` \"changing Run Args crosses the production gateway before PCR composition\" shows a Run-Arg change (a threshold) must re-execute through the gateway (`gatewayRuns` increments) and produces a different `runResultId`, whereas View Args never do; `pcr.test.ts:51-60,135-139` assert `'run' in pcr === false` and that PCR throws if asked to present \"a planned Tick that never ran.\" What a person actually sees, per Tick: `f3ecab3:src/lib/evidence-workbench/PcrInspectionHost.svelte` renders one Tick at a time (`TickInspection` component, line 86) with a `materializationView` selector whose full vocabulary is fixed in `f3ecab3:src/lib/evidence-workbench/pcrInspectionPlan.ts:1-12`: `['raw','bw','ownership','residue-after','composed','components','available','explained','unexplained','relationships']`, plus `zoom`, `showGrid`, `showReceipt` — i.e. per-Tick structured projections of pixel material (owned/muted/residue), not raw values. The host's own header text names the same View-Args/production-gateway split for the human reader: `PcrInspectionHost.svelte:89-94` — \"Projection-only MaterializationView / View Args never cross the production gateway,\" displayed next to the live `renderId`. The default entry specimen is fail-loud, not silently blank: `pcrInspectionPlan.ts:25-31` throws if the library isn't `'materialized'`, if the default PCR id or Tick id is missing, or if the default specimen is missing — \"default PCR inspection plan requires materialized computation,\" etc. Frozen-calculation identity shown alongside each Tick explicitly states its own limitation, matching pyto's `implementation_sha256` caveat: `f3ecab3:tests/unit/pcr.test.ts:33-37` — `identityScope: 'runtime-function-body'`, `limitation: 'called helpers, constants, templates, and assets are not covered'`.
storage: No storage backend, DuckDB, or content-addressing mechanism is introduced or discussed anywhere in this tip. `grep -ri duckdb` across the entire extracted tip returned zero hits. The Python `PxC` (`f3ecab3:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/core.py:46-93`) is an in-memory `dict[str, Any]` only — no serialization, no persistence, no revision/digest concept: `set()` just records `\"replacement\"` vs `\"new-address\"` write kind (`core.py:62-66`) and there is no `sha256`/digest field anywhere in the Python package. The TS `PCR` does carry a content-identity idea, but it is a run-result hash over already-produced testimony, not a storage backend: `f3ecab3:packages/alg/src/exec/pcr.ts:69-76` computes `runResultId = sha256HexSyncText(canonicalJson({planFingerprint, paramsHash, ticks: ...frozenTickIdentity}))`, and is explicit about what it does not cover: `pcr.ts:29-31,84-85` — \"Explicitly bounded: opaque PxC values are not silently claimed as content-frozen\" / `runResultIdentityLimitation: 'opaque PxC output values require an emitted Materialization'\". \"What was archived and why\" — nothing was archived in this tip; the only archival-adjacent note is `f3ecab3:packages/alg/src/stages/S0/exp/mermaid-pcr/README.md:23-24`: \"The combined S0-S1 graph and S0-S1.pcr.yaml are historical drafts, not inputs to this entry point,\" i.e. earlier PCR YAML kept as history but explicitly not live material. Missing entirely from this tip: any statement on per-namespace storage backend choice, S3-opposite specialized-backend design, or warm-start budget — those all belong to the pyto research docs (`ULTRACODE-WEEK.md` Reframings 2 and 5), not to this ChainSpot commit.
materialization_and_ticks: Tick shape matches pyto's `Tick -> Calculation[]` exactly and is the direct transfer source: Python `Tick` is `name` + ordered `calculations: list[Invocation]` (`f3ecab3:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/pcr.py:28-56`); `PCR.run()` iterates Ticks in declared order, and for each Tick emits one `TickTestimony(name, calculations)` (`pcr.py:135-177`), so a Tick is literally the unit at which \"its Calculations become observable\" (the origin.md phrase) — `PcrRun.ticks` is a tuple of these, returned alongside `results: dict[str, Any]` holding every invocation's actual value (`pcr.py:74-78,177`). This is a materially richer Tick than TS's: the Python `PcrRun.results` holds live values keyed by invocation id (`pcr.py:161-162,177`), whereas the TS `TickTestimony`/`Pcr` never carries values, only digests and a `runResultId` — consistent with the tick-observability-ledger's finding (`tick-observability-ledger.md:66`) that \"the actual computed Part value ... is only ever digested on the way to a file,\" and this ChainSpot-side tip does not close that gap either: no materializer function exists in it, only the authoring/testimony layer. Declaration-order execution and the writer-uniqueness invariant are enforced identically on both sides: Python `PCR.calc` raises \"multiple writers\" (`pcr.py:118-123`) and duplicate-id (`pcr.py:109-110`); TS compiler enforces the same plus forward-dependency/cycle rejection (`compiler.ts:69-80,93`, \"forward dependency or cycle\"), and TS execution is declaration-order per `f3ecab3:packages/alg/src/stages/S0/exp/mermaid-pcr/README.md:26-27` (\"declaration-order execution ... direct function-result arrows\"). PCR-as-non-engine is stated three times independently in this tip, at increasing levels of force: Python README (\"This is intentionally not a second ChainSpot executor... ChainSpot/PxC remains the intended execution owner,\" `experiments/quick-anno-python/README.md:7`), the mermaid-pcr README (\"runner.ts is an isolated experimental async interpreter... it is not integrated with shared PQL, Stage routing, browser inspection or S2,\" `mermaid-pcr/README.md:31-32`), and the TS `Pcr` type's own docstring (\"PCR has deliberately no run() method,\" `pcr.ts:17-21`) plus the test assertion `'run' in pcr === false` (`pcr.test.ts:60,132`).
receipts_and_telemetry: Python testimony shape (the receipt): `CalculationTestimony(id, calculation, inputs, args, into)` where `inputs` is a `dict[str,str]` of `\"px:<address>\"`/`\"fn:<id>\"` reference strings, never values (`f3ecab3:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/pcr.py:60-65,149-157,166-174`) — this is address/provenance-only testimony, matching pyto's own `testimony.json` shape (per the ledger, row 26) rather than a value-bearing receipt. No `duration_ms`, no digest, no timestamp field exists anywhere in the Python package — telemetry as pyto defines it (`Reframing 2`'s `duration_ms` + result digests) is entirely absent from this tip; it is a pure authoring/composition proof, not an instrumented run. The TS side (the transfer source) does carry telemetry-shaped fields the Python has not yet picked up: `TickTestimony` in `f3ecab3:tests/unit/pcr.test.ts:29-48` has `startedAtMs`, `durationMs`, `declaredConsumes`/`actualConsumes` vs `declaredProduces`/`actualProduces` (divergence-visible, matching pyto's `shadowed_inputs`/`actual_consumes` receipt fields), `writes: [{address, kind}]`, `probes: [{name, value}]`, and `frozenCalculations: [{address, implementationHash, identityScope, limitation}]` — i.e. the TS receipt already has the digest+timing+identity-scope shape pyto's `Reframing 2` seam (`PcrRun.observations`) is trying to add to Python. \"Run Args\" vs \"View Args\" is the tip's clearest telemetry/provenance distinction, stated as a test name: `pcr.test.ts:74` \"changing Run Args crosses the production gateway before PCR composition\" (production-affecting) vs `pcr.test.ts:63` \"changing View Args changes only render identity\" (inspection-only, never re-executes) — this is a stronger, code-enforced version of pyto's open `{?} ObservationSeam` question about keeping digests out of consumer-visible testimony bytes.
reusable_now: Port `graph.py`'s Pcr authoring surface (Part/Calculation reference normalization) as-is or near-as-is: it is a working, tested, dependency-free Python implementation of exactly the PxC/PCR composition shape pyto/src/pyto already has, with one difference worth adopting — Pcr.calc() in graph.py takes `tick, call` as positional args and `**inputs` as PartRef|ValueRef, producing a JSON-serializable `to_pcr_dict()` with explicit `{kind:'px'|'fn', ref}` bindings (f3ecab3:packages/quick_anno_py/chainspot_quick_anno/graph.py:89-114) — this is a cleaner declarative export format than pyto's current retain.py sidecar approach and could be compared directly against pyto Day 2's retain.py schema choice.

Adopt the fn./px. two-namespace enforcement pyto's own Calculation already has (core.py:33-34 raises if address doesn't start with 'fn.') paired with the TS compiler's stronger rule that a Part can never write directly to another Part (compiler.ts:73, 'PxC-to-PxC edges require a Calculation') — pyto's Part class has no equivalent enforced rule today; this closing rule could be ported into pyto/src/pyto/core.py as a cheap addressing-discipline improvement.

Port the View-Args-vs-Run-Args split (pcr.ts:90-92, pcr.test.ts:63-133) directly into pyto's PCR/PcrRun: pyto's `{?} ObservationSeam` question (keep digests off asdict(tick) bytes) is exactly what this pattern already solves in production TS code — a `pcrRenderId(run, viewArgs)` pure function separate from the run identity, with a test asserting viewArgs never changes runResultId. This is a ready-made resolution to pyto's open question, not just an analogy.

Adopt the mermaid-pcr Svelte MaterializationView vocabulary (pcrInspectionPlan.ts:1-12: raw/bw/ownership/residue-after/composed/components/available/explained/unexplained/relationships) as a starting menu for pyto's still-unbuilt Tick materializer (tick-observability-ledger.md section 3) — it is a proven, human-reviewed set of per-Tick pixel projections rather than an invented one.

Reuse the fail-loud default-plan pattern (pcrInspectionPlan.ts:25-44: throw naming exactly which piece is missing — pcr id, tick id, specimen id, or 'not materialized') as the shape for pyto's Tick viewer's own default/entrypoint guard, satisfying the 'no CLI or command that runs a PCR and writes a sheet' gap named in tick-observability-ledger.md:83.

commit_message: Add unrun S0 and S1 Mermaid PCR review proof
addressing: Root/prefix rule, enforced mechanically: every graph node must be `fn.*` or `px.*` or the compiler rejects it (b5a6ae0:packages/alg/src/stages/S0/exp/mermaid-pcr/compiler.ts:32, :46-47). Addresses are dotted paths that encode stage, experimental-vs-clean status, module and kind before the leaf name, e.g. a per-module ROOT constant: `const ROOT = 'px.s1.exp.maskComponents.part.' as const;` (b5a6ae0:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/mask-components/index.ts:8), used to build every Part's own `address` field (`type PartAddress = \`px.s1.exp.maskComponents.part.${string}\`;`, index.ts:21). Each segment discriminates (stage S1, `exp` marking non-canonical experimental status, the owning module `maskComponents`, the kind `part`) rather than being generic — the closest concrete instance found of the owner's "meaningful root/segment" rule, though no file states the rule itself; it is only enacted in code. S1's public output surface is a frozen, named list rather than a wildcard: `export const S1_OUTPUT_ADDRESSES = ['px.badges.objects','px.badges.px','px.badges.muted','px.remaining.afterBadges'] as const;` (b5a6ae0:packages/alg/src/stages/S0/exp/mermaid-pcr/compare.ts:3-7), and `outputAddresses` parity is checked against exactly that set. Cross-Stage alignment is a first-class field, not inferred: every raster Part carries `coordinateFrameId: typeof S0_CROPPED_IMAGE_ADDRESS` (mask-components/index.ts:31) pinning it to the address of the frame it was measured in, plus `sourceAddress`/`sourceTickId` provenance fields. No dynamic registration of addresses at runtime was found in this tip: the graph source (S0.mmd/S1.mmd) is the sole author of which addresses exist, compiled once into YAML (`compileMermaidPcr`), and the interpreter (runner.ts) only reads/writes addresses the compiler already validated — \"declaration order is executable order; reject forward dependencies, including via PxC\" (compiler.ts:58 comment). No `mount`, or PxC-storage-backend-selection-by-prefix language was found tied to addressing in this tip's added docs/code (the two `namespace` hits, in scripts/chainspot-lab/README.md:185 and .task/LAB-SCOPE-V0.md:102, are about UI \"Search Page\" overlay namespaces on a raster, unrelated to px./fn. addressing) — missing.

(node-sink.ts:4-9), with the same sha256-per-artifact (node-sink.ts:25) and `uri: \`file://${filePath}\`` (node-sink.ts:30). `ArtifactRef` is documented as a "Content-addressed reference to an artifact the sink has stored. `uri` is sink-defined ... the exec core never interprets it, only carries it through the receipt." (contract.ts:90-95), and dimensions are opt-in, never inferred: "A consumer receiving undefined MUST NOT infer dimensions from byte length -- decline to rasterize instead." (contract.ts:110-111). This is a working instance of pyto's `{?} StorageKinds` thesis (a facade with a kind-selected backend, "precise opposite of S3") — but keyed by a declared artifact `kind` enum (rgba, mask, scalarField, componentSet, badgeEvidence, m1/m2Representation, polyline, measurementTable; contract.ts:77-88) and by explicit sink choice, not by address prefix. Receipts are append-only JSONL, not a single retained.json or any database. No other storage backend (sqlite, a graph store, etc.) appears in this tip.
materialization_and_ticks: Two independent Tick-execution mechanisms are present. (1) The production-shaped one, `executeCompiledPlan`/`executeCompiledPlanAsync` (packages/alg/src/exec/gateway.ts:124-219): for each `OperationSpec` it freezes calculation identity via `freezeCalculations` — hashing `Function.prototype.toString.call(binding.calculate)` into `implementationHash` and erroring loudly if bound calculations disagree with declared `fn.*` addresses (gateway.ts:57-81); tracks real access with `trackAccess(board, op)` yielding `{tracked, consumed, produced, writes}`; times each op (`durationMs = now() - startedAtMs`); throws on declared-vs-actual mismatch only when `op.accessConformance === 'exact'` (`assertAccessConformance`, gateway.ts:103-122) — conformance checking is opt-in per operation, not global; computes generic "shape probes" — "for every slot an operation actually produced, record its element count when the value is array-like" (gateway.ts:83-91, `shapeProbes`), a disclosed partial telemetry ("fine-grained score distributions still ride ctx.measure/UnitTrace at unit level; Receipt.probes carries op-level candidate-count shape instead.", gateway.ts:90-91); and extracts artifacts through injected `artifactExtractors`, written via the sink. (2) The experimental one built for this proof, `executeMermaidYaml` (packages/alg/src/stages/S0/exp/mermaid-pcr/runner.ts:27-56), explicitly marked non-canonical: "Experimental interpreter for compiler output. Actual values remain in the returned record, never in a PxC run-record address. This is not yet the shared PQL executor." (runner.ts:25-26). It walks compiled Ticks/Calculations in order, rejects duplicate occurrence ids ("Duplicate occurrence '${calculation.id}'.", runner.ts:36), enforces argument/binding non-collision ("Argument shadows '${name}'.", runner.ts:38) — resolving pyto's `{?} SilentRules` shadow concern the loud-failure way JS already does — and on failure raises `MermaidExecutionError` carrying the partial `RunRecord` with every prior call's status intact (runner.ts:20-24, 49-52), which `run.ts` persists to `failed-run.v8` + `failure.json` on catch (run.ts:47-51), retaining the successful prefix exactly as pyto's Day 2 replay/tamper discipline wants. Materialization proper (turning run values into inspectable files) happens only in the CLI, not the library: `run.ts` pulls `px.course.canonicalPixels`, `px.badges.px`, `px.badges.muted`, `px.remaining.afterBadges` back out of PxC by address and writes them as PNGs (run.ts:26-39), plus a binary V8-serialized trace ("Binary trace retains typed arrays and shared object identity without giant JSON arrays.", run.ts:24) and a JSON `receipt.json`. Neither mechanism nor the checklist claims this ran: REFINE.md's checklist is entirely unchecked ("- [ ] Compile S0 and S1 independently...", REFINE.md:7-24), stating "Not completed by this prototype: shared PQL integration, Stage selection/routing, browser traversal, S2 compatibility or promotion." (REFINE.md:26-28).
receipts_and_telemetry: The canonical receipt shape (packages/alg/src/exec/contract.ts:127-141) is: `interface Receipt { opId; frozenCalculations: FrozenCalculation[]; startedAtMs; durationMs; declaredConsumes; declaredProduces; actualConsumes; actualProduces; writes: PxWriteTestimony[]; probes: Probe[]; artifacts: ArtifactRef[] }`, commented: "Per-operation execution record. `declared*` comes from the OperationSpec; `actual*` comes from what the operation really touched on the evidence board while running. The two diverging is a conformance failure the gateway surfaces rather than silently accepting." (contract.ts:121-125). `FrozenCalculation` self-limits its own claim: `identityScope: 'runtime-function-body'` with `limitation: 'called helpers, constants, templates, and assets are not covered'` (contract.ts:60-67) — the same limitation pyto's ULTRACODE-WEEK plan already names for `implementation_sha256` (`{?} CacheInvalidation`). `PxWriteTestimony.kind` is a closed union `'new-address' | 'refinement' | 'replacement'` (contract.ts:71-74), making a colliding write a distinguishable, visible event rather than a silent overwrite — directly answering part of pyto's open `{?} SilentRules`. `Probe { name: string; value: number }` (contract.ts:116-119) is the entire telemetry unit: one named scalar per probe, populated today only by `shapeProbes`' array-length heuristic (gateway.ts:92-101) — telemetry here is shape-of-output counts, not timing distributions or perceptual scores. The concrete on-disk receipt this commit exercises is `review/s1-ownership/receipt.json`, shaped `{rule, reviewMarginPx, marginPurpose, partition, source, executionMs, owned, muted, remaining, total, perBadge:[{id, number, bbox, components, unaccountedButOwned, excluded}, ...]}` (b5a6ae0:review/s1-ownership/receipt.json:1-29+) — an accounting receipt (pixel counts that must sum and partition exhaustively), not the `Receipt`/`Tick` shape above; its README states the limit explicitly: "These checks prove accounting, not that every assigned pixel is semantically correct." (review/s1-ownership/README.md:20). `run.ts`'s own `receipt.json` for the S0/S1 Mermaid proof is a third, narrower shape: `{ok, input, checks, badges:[{id,reading,unaccountedButOwned}], calls:[...merged S0+S1 CallRecords minus inputs/output], inspection: 'actual-runs.v8 preserves actual inputs/outputs; masks show exact sets separately.'}` (run.ts:40-44) — values are deliberately excluded from the JSON receipt and pushed into a binary V8 sidecar, mirroring pyto's own digest-vs-value split (`Receipt.result_sha256` only, values live in `PcrRun.results`).

commit_message: Investigate source instances behind S1 right-side badge residue
what_it_is: The diff against main on branch lab/pxc-root-mounts is a large accumulated branch (hundreds of files: skills, workflows, docs, a whole S0-S3 CV pipeline, a Svelte staging app, an evidence-workbench/Storybook viewer, LAB CLI) but only a small, coherent slice is about PxC root mounts / PCR: a new `PxCRootMounts` map that mounts whole already-built `PxC` worlds (one per course image) under an external root id, a new `packages/alg/src/exec/pcr.ts` that composes already-executed Tick testimony into a frozen, non-executing `Pcr` object for a Storybook/staging viewer (`/lab/pcr`), and a `warm-dev-pxc-roots.mjs`/CI workflow that mounts every dev-corpus course's post-S1 PxC and measures cold-start time. The commit message itself ("Investigate source instances behind S1 right-side badge residue") describes unrelated badge-residue work also included in the same branch tip; the PxC-mounts/PCR material was evidently added on earlier commits of this branch and is what the task asked to mine.
addressing: DECIDED: the mount root is deliberately kept OUTSIDE the PxC semantic address space rather than becoming a namespace prefix inside it. mounts.ts:3-7: "A root mounted above an ordinary PxC. The root is intentionally external to PxC's semantic address space: values remain px.* and calculations remain fn.* inside every mounted world." The root id is "currently ImgID" (mounts.ts:11), i.e. one root per course/image, and `get()`/`mount()` do no rewriting: mounts.ts:15 "Return the exact PxC mounted at root; no address rewriting occurs." The test that pins this down is named for exactly the owner's connection concern — pxcRootMounts.test.ts:6 "keeps ImgID outside the PxC address space" — and asserts the negative directly: pxcRootMounts.test.ts:16-17 `expect(dash.has('px.DashsTrack.s1.badges')).toBe(false)` / `expect(north.has('px.NorthPark.s1.badges')).toBe(false)`, i.e. the root name is explicitly never spliced into an address. Connection is instead achieved by identity repetition, not hierarchy: the same flat address (e.g. `px.s1.badges` or `px.course.canonicalPixels`) is independently resolvable inside every mounted root, which is what the batch warmer calls out as the point: warm-dev-pxc-roots.mjs:60 "// Wide access proof: one semantic address, independently resolved in every mounted world." and its emitted report literally states the rule: warm-dev-pxc-roots.mjs:69 `rootSemantics: '<ImgID>/{px.*,fn.*}'`, `addressMutation: false`. `roots()`/`entries()`/`slice()` (mounts.ts:17-22) give stable insertion-order, cheap grouped projection across roots without cloning: mounts.ts:21 "Make a cheap root-level slice; mounted PxCs themselves are shared." This is a different answer than a namespace-prefixed address (`px.<root>.s1.badges`), and it is a live counterpoint to pyto's open `{?} StorageKinds` framing of "backend chosen by address prefix" (questions.md:179-184) — here the chosen mechanism is an external mount registry keyed by a meaningful id (the image/course identity) with the address space itself staying uniform and unrewritten across mounts, so "connection" comes from address-identity reuse across worlds rather than from a root segment carrying discriminating meaning inside each address. Adjacent but separate: the LAB CLI's "Search Pages" are explicitly called out the same way — named overlay namespaces over one shared raster, not copies: `.task/LAB-SCOPE-V0.md:102` "Search Pages are named overlay namespaces on the same canonical raster, allowing scratch/notes/final surfaces without duplicating image data," and `scripts/chainspot-lab/README.md:185` "Pages are visibility/mutation namespaces, not raster copies." No explicit rule is stated anywhere in this tip for how a root id must be chosen or must discriminate beyond "non-empty" (mounts.ts:30 `if (!root) throw new Error('PxC mounts: root id must be non-empty.')`) and "one PxC per root, no silent remount" (mounts.ts:31-34 throws if a different PxC is remounted at the same root) — there is no stated rule that a root must itself carry semantic connection the way the owner's "wasted log(N) potential" statement asks; it is treated as an opaque, already-meaningful key (an image id) rather than a designed address segment.
viewer_and_pcr_render: Per-Tick, and it is explicitly execution-free: pcr.ts:17-21 "Storybook-facing composition of already-executed Tick testimony. PCR has deliberately no run() method: the production gateway is the only execution authority and hands this function the receipts it already produced." `composePcr()` (pcr.ts:51-88) takes a `PcrSpec{id,title,tickIds}` plus the plan and the already-produced `TickTestimony[]`, and only assembles `{operation, testimony}` pairs per tick — it throws if a listed Tick "never ran" (pcr.ts:66, exercised by pcr.test.ts:135-139) or is named twice (pcr.ts:61). Identity of the whole PCR is a sha256 over plan fingerprint + params hash + a frozen projection of each tick's testimony (pcr.ts:70-76, `frozenTickIdentity` at pcr.ts:35-49), explicitly bounded: pcr.ts:29-31 "Explicitly bounded: opaque PxC values are not silently claimed as content-frozen" / `runResultIdentityLimitation: 'opaque PxC output values require an emitted Materialization'`. What a person sees is per-Tick structure, not raw values by default: the viewer route `/lab/pcr` (a Storybook-reused molecule) opens on a checked default plan — pcrInspectionPlan.ts:15-23 `DEFAULT_PCR_INSPECTION_PLAN = {pcrId:'badge-pcr', tickId:'badgeStage.masks', specimenId:'badge-0', materializationView:'composed', zoom:6, showGrid:false, showReceipt:true}` — and a set of named `MaterializationView`s the user can flip between: pcrInspectionPlan.ts:1-12 `PCR_MATERIALIZATION_VIEWS = ['raw','bw','ownership','residue-after','composed','components','available','explained','unexplained','relationships']`. Loading the default plan is fail-loud, not silently degraded: pcrInspectionPlan.ts:25-31 "Fail the staging build instead of publishing a blank or drifted default plan," checked against materialized PCR/Tick/specimen identity actually present. The render is fed by `library.pcrs`/`library.specimens` from a server-side `materializeBadgeSpecimens()` load function (+page.server.ts:1-8), then `PcrInspectionHost.svelte` selects the named PCR and Tick (`library.pcrs.find(...)`, PcrInspectionHost.svelte:20,30) and renders a `TickInspection` panel (testimony) beside a separate, clearly labeled "Projection-only MaterializationView" panel whose header states the boundary explicitly: PcrInspectionHost.svelte:90-92 "Projection-only MaterializationView" / "View Args never cross the production gateway". Changing the materialization view (zoom, grid, which projection) only changes a separate render-identity hash, never the run identity: pcr.ts:90-93 "View identity is a pure projection of a frozen PCR; it cannot execute CV," proven by pcr.test.ts:63-72 (`pcrRenderId` differs across `{zoom:2}` vs `{zoom:4}` while `pcr.runResultId` stays identical). The whole staging surface's purpose is stated directly: src/lib/evidence-workbench/README.md:27-30 "`/lab/pcr` reuses the Storybook inspection molecules against the same materialized computation. It opens with the checked `DEFAULT_PCR_INSPECTION_PLAN`... The staging build fails loudly if the corpus is absent or any default PCR, Tick, or specimen identity has drifted." Note a second, unrelated sense of "PCR" appears in this branch: docs/handoffs/BADGE-PCR-DISCOVERY-SCRIPT.md:1-25 uses "PCR" to mean the git-commit narrative/history structure of the badge investigation ("the useful PCR is the one so faithful to the actual algorithm that the missing counters become obvious accidentally," line 25), not the `Pcr` render object — the two usages should not be conflated when porting vocabulary.
storage: No DuckDB, no external database, and no disk-backed content-addressed store appear anywhere in this tip's diff (grep for "duckdb" across the extracted tree returned nothing) — storage stays in-memory. `PxCRootMounts` (mounts.ts:25-53) is a plain `Map<PxCRootId, PxC>`; mounting is "one already-materialized world" (mounts.ts:11), i.e. the store holds whole `PxC` objects (themselves `Map`-backed `ExecBoard`s, board.ts:59-79), not individual serialized rows. `PxC` itself (board.ts:38-45) is described as "PxC's browser-safe address space," with `fork()` explicitly a snapshot ("Snapshot addresses and registered functions; immutable Part values remain shared," board.ts:41) — copy-on-fork, not persistence. What is archived is receipts and content-addressed artifact references, not raw Parts: `ArtifactRef` (contract.ts:97-105) is "Content-addressed reference to an artifact the sink has stored... `uri` is sink-defined (a file:// path from the Node sink, an in-memory handle from a browser/collector sink) — the exec core never interprets it, only carries it through the receipt," and the contract file states the boundary up front: contract.ts:6-9 "R1 (browser-safe core): everything below describes DATA. Writing an artifact or receipt to disk is the job of an INJECTED sink the caller hands to executeCompiledPlan — never something a type here performs." So "storage" in this tip is a pluggable sink for artifact bytes (Node vs browser/in-memory) plus an in-process root-mount registry for whole PxC worlds; there is no backend-per-kind facade (raster/graph/JSON) as pyto's `{?} StorageKinds` proposes, and no persistence across process restarts is implemented — `warm-dev-pxc-roots.mjs` rebuilds every course's PxC from the corpus each run (lines 32-58) rather than reading a persisted store. One retained-caching convention does appear at the PCR-spec level: S0.pcr.yaml:15-16 declares `last: cache: FullImage`, i.e. the yaml names which upstream value the last Tick should re-cache — but no code in this tip's tree consumes `S0.pcr.yaml` (grep for the filename outside itself found no reader), so this is a documented/aspirational schema, not a wired mechanism.
materialization_and_ticks: The Tick/testimony shape is materialized as `Receipt`, and `TickTestimony` is a direct type alias of it: contract.ts:143-147 "A Tick is the existing gateway Receipt understood as inspection testimony: exact addresses in, frozen calculations, exact addresses out. It adds no execution authority and deliberately has no run() method." / `export type TickTestimony = Receipt;`. A `Receipt` (contract.ts:118-141) carries `opId`, `frozenCalculations` (each `FrozenCalculation`: `address`, `implementationHash`, and an honestly-scoped `identityScope:'runtime-function-body'` with `limitation:'called helpers, constants, templates, and assets are not covered'`, contract.ts:65-68 — the same scope-limitation language pyto's `implementation_sha256` carries), `startedAtMs`/`durationMs`, `declaredConsumes`/`declaredProduces` vs `actualConsumes`/`actualProduces`, `writes: PxWriteTestimony[]` classified as `'new-address'|'refinement'|'replacement'` (contract.ts:73-76, exercised in pxcTick.test.ts:38-54), `probes: Probe[]` (named numeric observations, contract.ts:108-110), and `artifacts: ArtifactRef[]`. Access is tracked live against the board (`trackAccess`, exercised in pxcTick.test.ts): a missing read throws by Tick name — pxcTick.test.ts:33-35 `"PxC: Tick 'test.double' read missing address 'px.test.missing'."` — and an opt-in `accessConformance:'exact'` mode refuses undeclared traffic instead of recording a plausible receipt: pxcTick.test.ts:114-139, throwing `/extra reads=\[px\.test\.hiddenInput\]/`, and separately refuses a calculation bound under the wrong `fn.*` address (pxcTick.test.ts:94-112, `/calculation bindings disagree/`). This is a concrete, already-shipped implementation of pyto's open `{?} SilentRules` question (should pcr.py raise at declaration/access instead of failing only at run) — here JS already fails loud on exactly that shadow case. A full multi-Tick chain is demonstrated end to end in s0IntakePcr.test.ts:45-49: `run.pcr.ticks.map(t=>t.operation.id)` equals `['source.decodeFullImage','source.cropUDiscChrome','source.cacheFullImage']`, i.e. three real Ticks (decode, crop, cache) each producing its own testimony, composed into one `Pcr`. `PCR.mermaid()`-equivalent visibility is not present in this tip (no mermaid export found in the diffed files); the render is purely the Storybook/staging JSON+HTML view described above. The batch warmer (`warm-dev-pxc-roots.mjs`) is the closest thing to a materialization-observability harness for the mounts themselves: it times mounting every dev-corpus course's post-S1 world against `TARGET_MS = 40_000` / `HARD_MS = 55_000` (lines 9-10) — a much looser cold-start budget than pyto's stated 5000 ms CV target (questions.md WarmupBudget), worth flagging as a discrepancy if this convention is ported.
receipts_and_telemetry: The `Receipt`/`TickTestimony` shape (contract.ts:118-141, quoted above) is the telemetry unit: per-invocation `durationMs`/`startedAtMs`, declared-vs-actual consumes/produces, typed writes, named numeric `Probe`s, and content-addressed `ArtifactRef`s. `ArtifactRef` (contract.ts:97-105) is `{id, kind, sha256, uri, dims?}` where `kind: ArtifactKind` is a closed enum — contract.ts:78-89: `'rgba'|'mask'|'scalarField'|'orientationField'|'componentSet'|'candidateSet'|'badgeEvidence'|'m1Representation'|'m2Representation'|'polyline'|'measurementTable'` — and `dims?: RasterDims{width,height}` is present only for raster kinds "whose extractor knew the shape," with an explicit non-inference rule: contract.ts:93-96 "A consumer receiving undefined MUST NOT infer dimensions from byte length -- decline to rasterize instead." This `ArtifactKind`+`dims` pair is a direct, already-built answer to the gap pyto's tick-observability-ledger.md section 3 item 4 names as missing ("No way to tell an image Part from a scalar Part... no kind, dtype, or renderer tag"). At the mount/warm level, telemetry is a flat JSON report: warm-dev-pxc-roots.mjs:68-78 `{rootSemantics, addressMutation, mountedRoots, targetMs, hardMs, elapsedMs, withinTarget, rows:[{label,root,input,croppedPx}], wideCanonicalPixels:[{root,label,widthPx,heightPx}]}`, written to disk and uploaded as a CI artifact by `.github/workflows/pxc-root-warm.yml:29-37`. `Pcr` itself carries a schema tag for future evolution — pcr.ts:23 `readonly schema: 'chainspot-pcr@1'` — a versioned-schema convention pyto's `testimony.json`/`retained.json` do not currently carry.
reusable_now: Port the mounts.ts pattern directly for pyto's namespace/mount question (questions.md {?} StorageKinds, {?} PortableKernel): an external, non-address-rewriting root registry (`mount(root,pxc)/has/get/roots/entries/slice`) that keeps every mounted PxC's addresses flat and uniform (px.*/fn.*) while the root id (an opaque, already-meaningful key like an image/course id) lives outside the address — a concrete, tested alternative to choosing a backend by address prefix.

Port the ArtifactKind + RasterDims convention (contract.ts:78-96) into pyto's Part/materializer design to close the exact gap named in tick-observability-ledger.md section 3 item 4 (no way to dispatch a Part to a pixel renderer vs json.dumps).

Port the Receipt-field shape (declared vs actual consumes/produces, typed writes new-address/refinement/replacement, frozenCalculations with an honestly-scoped identityScope+limitation string, probes, content-addressed artifacts) as the target shape for pyto's Tick materializer output — it is close to a drop-in match for pyto's existing Receipt/CalculationTestimony fields plus the two things pyto is missing (artifact kind/dims, write-kind classification).

Port the accessConformance:'exact' / trackAccess fail-loud-on-undeclared-traffic pattern (pxcTick.test.ts) as a working precedent for resolving pyto's open {?} SilentRules the way the owner's plan already flags JS as doing (raise at declaration/access, not just at run).

Port the PCR/render-identity separation (pcr.ts:90-93, pcr.test.ts:63-72): a `pcrRenderId(pcr, viewArgs)` hashed separately from `pcr.runResultId`, so changing a materialization/view setting never re-executes or re-hashes the underlying computation — directly useful for pyto's Day 3 Tick viewer to avoid conflating render state with run identity.

Port the fail-loud default-plan convention (pcrInspectionPlan.ts:25-44, requireDefaultPcrInspectionPlan) for pyto's viewer: assert the default PCR/Tick/specimen actually exist in the materialized library and throw naming exactly what drifted, rather than rendering blank.
Adopt the schema-version tag convention (`schema: 'chainspot-pcr@1'`, pcr.ts:23) on pyto's testimony.json/retained.json.

Note but do not port as-is: the 40s/55s PxC-root warm budget (warm-dev-pxc-roots.mjs:9-10) is far looser than pyto's 5000ms target and should not be copied as a budget figure, only as a warm-report shape.

addressing:
This tip never uses PxC's Tick/Calculation address grammar as pyto defines it (`fn.*`, `px.*` per pyto's own docs), but the S1 experiment tree (packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md) shows a real, running instance of address-as-storage-key that is directly comparable: "The caller receives results and the input PxC stores them at px.pql.<Stage>.results." (chainspot:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md:12) and feature-discovery's dependency declaration reads addresses as preconditions: "Requires warm px.s1.exp.badgeAssembly.badgeCandidates and px.s1.discovery.labels." (chainspot:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/feature-discovery/REVIEW.md:4). experiments/parts-inspector/README.md shows a third namespace, `px.view.*`, reserved for UI-only state that never triggers computation: "Selection, visibility, isolation, and framing use `px.view.partsInspector`; those controls do not invoke Calculations." (chainspot:experiments/parts-inspector/README.md:3-5). So the *root* segments actually in use are `px.pql.<Stage>.results`, `px.s1.<...>`, `px.view.<...>` — each root names a distinct kind of thing (a Stage's declared outputs, a specific exp module's Parts, UI-only view state), which is a working example of the owner's "the root must carry connection, not a generic label" rule, though none of these docs states that rule explicitly — it is inferred from the naming, not asserted.

The clearest explicit addressing statement in the tip is about content addressing, not namespace roots: .task/CHSPT-82.md specifies a canonical composite's identity as a hash over its bytes, not a hand-assigned label: "canonical composite materialization: real pixel flattening (Node-runnable, no canvas) + content-addressed `imageId` = sha256 over `[u32be widthPx][u32be heightPx][raw RGBA bytes]`, documented and pinned by a known-tiny-composite unit test." (chainspot:.task/CHSPT-82.md:270-271). That is a genuine "address carries connection" instance — the address IS the content, so two identical composites from different pipelines collide on purpose and become the same document — directly resonant with Reframing 4's "content addressing as the document identity" for PxC (pyto/research/ULTRACODE-WEEK.md:83).

Search Pages give a second, non-computational namespace convention worth reading against pyto's mounts: "Search Pages are named overlay namespaces on the same canonical raster, allowing scratch/notes/final surfaces without duplicating image data." (chainspot:.task/LAB-SCOPE-V0.md:102) and "Pages are visibility/mutation namespaces, not raster copies." (chainspot:scripts/chainspot-lab/README.md:185). No Page name is privileged: "Page names and retained/promoted semantics remain user-controlled and dogfoodable; no specific Page name is privileged in the state model." (chainspot:.task/LAB-SCOPE-V0.md:104) — an anti-generic-root discipline in spirit, applied to a different address space (raster overlays, not PxC Parts).

The matrix-review experiment states an explicit PxC addressing formula, closest of anything in this tip to a "how addresses connect" rule: "LAB stores actual calibration and pose profiles at PxC addresses keyed by source bytes, frame, seed, masks, sensor parameters and calculation revision." (chainspot:experiments/dashs-track-edge-sensing/matrix-review/README.md:23) — i.e. the address key is a tuple of everything that could change the value's meaning, so that "identical profiles can feed different predicates without counting as independent evidence" (chainspot:experiments/dashs-track-edge-sensing/LAB-BROAD-TESTING-PROPOSAL.md:57-58). That is a concrete, load-bearing definition of what a discriminating address segment must include — directly transferable to pyto's own address design. No explicit "root must not be generic" rule is ever written down in this tip; that owner statement postdates it and is not itself present in the ChainSpot repo. Missing: any mount/prefix-to-backend routing table, any registration step for a namespace, any statement that addressing is unregistered by design (pyto's own "no registration" framing is absent here — must be recorded as missing per instructions).
viewer_and_pcr_render:
badge-assembly/REVIEW.md documents a real, working PCR: "PrincipleComponentRender.yaml owns the full experimental S1 order and arguments. The Stage factory prepares inputs/registers implementations and delegates to the shared runner." (chainspot:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md:7) — confirming pyto's PrincipleComponentRender naming is not a pyto invention but a live ChainSpot artifact (a YAML file). Its Ticks/forks are PxC forks, not named Tick objects: "A PxC fork snapshots slot and function maps. It shares immutable values, including raster buffers. Each run's writes stay in its own fork. A following Stage can consume the chosen result's pxc." (chainspot:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md:11). Per-invocation testimony is retained but not yet joined into a per-Tick view, exactly the gap tick-observability-ledger.md section 3 names for pyto: "Runs retain declared call, actualCall, effective args, inputs, and outputs for differentiation. This is recorded material, not a comparison score." (chainspot:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md:12). What a person actually sees is described concretely: "The shared browser-safe JS renderer produces SVG from exact pixel membership. The HTML inspector reads Calculation outputs, lets the user select an item and toggle its component Parts, and exports the same SVG projection. View controls perform no CV calculations." (chainspot:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md:14) — pixels/masks rendered as colored SVG regions, selectable per candidate, Parts toggle-able, and the viewer is read-only (never computes). experiments/parts-inspector/README.md gives the fed values precisely: "`receipt.json` records the actual Default run: 3 Ticks, 9 Calculations, 952 black components, 176 white components, 18 candidates, no incomplete assemblies. `candidate.svg` shows the first candidate with a possible loop; `candidate.png` is that SVG rasterized at 768 density. Amber is plate material, cyan border, white digit material, pink possible loop, and gray unselected pixels." (chainspot:experiments/parts-inspector/README.md:18-22). This is a Tick-count-labeled render fed by a receipt.json and a PxC seeded with saved raster bytes: "The staging `/parts` page seeds PxC with exact saved S0 raster bytes and runs the existing S1 YAML once." (chainspot:experiments/parts-inspector/README.md:3-4). A UI-decision worth porting: "Sam's resolved preference: selecting another result starts with every Part visible, including Parts shared with a previously viewed result." (chainspot:experiments/parts-inspector/README.md:31-32) — a default-visible-until-hidden rule for a multi-candidate viewer. The tip also records, via docs/unported/engine-dev72-lineage.md, a full post-mortem of an EARLIER browser receipt viewer (T5) that was built and then explicitly rejected for pyto/ChessLab-style porting: "T5's receipt viewer disagrees with T6's receipt shape, and nothing catches it... The viewer survives only because it renders `work` as `
{json(...)}
`" (chainspot:docs/unported/engine-dev72-lineage.md:339-345), and the verdict: "T5's receipt viewer (677 lines of Svelte) — its data model is wrong against the shipped receipt. Rebuild from the real `Receipt` type." (chainspot:docs/unported/engine-dev72-lineage.md:556-558) and the regeneration note: "Reconcile the receipt `work` shape before writing a viewer. One definition, one fixture, generated from a real sink run rather than hand-authored." (chainspot:docs/unported/engine-dev72-lineage.md:532-534). This is a direct, concrete lesson for pyto's Day-3 tick-viewer: freeze the receipt shape from a real run before writing the viewer against it, never hand-author the fixture. Missing: no per-Stage (vs per-Tick) toggle is described anywhere in this tip; nothing states what "per Stage" would show differently from "per Tick."
storage:
The tip's dominant storage decision is documented as a deliberate archival act, not a backend choice: docs/unported/README.md explains the whole 11-file docs/unported/** addition as "we made a deliberate choice to **abandon the code and keep the knowledge**. Ten extractors read the old branches read-only and wrote down, in prose, what each piece of work detects, why it exists, what pixels it looks at, every magic number it depends on, and what evidence (if any) proves it works... The old repo stays read-only forever; when this machine is reset, these files are what survives." (chainspot:docs/unported/README.md:6). This is the ChainSpot analogue of pyto's "archived because it was too slow" pattern ({?} WarmupBudget, DuckDB) — here the archival trigger is an irreconcilable directory-layout fork, not a latency budget, but the pattern (keep the knowledge, discard the code, mark verdicts explicitly) is directly reusable. Concretely one branch is marked for deletion with justification: "`lab/dev72-algorithm` should simply be deleted — it contains no file and no hunk that `engine/dev72` does not already have." (chainspot:docs/unported/engine-dev72-lineage.md:570-571), and another spec is marked discard: "[`lab-render-evidence.md`] ... **discard** ... Strict subset of `engine/dev72`" (chainspot:docs/unported/README.md:14).

Content addressing appears once, precisely: a canonical pixel composite's identity is its own hash, per .task/CHSPT-82.md: "canonical composite materialization: real pixel flattening (Node-runnable, no canvas) + content-addressed `imageId` = sha256 over `[u32be widthPx][u32be heightPx][raw RGBA bytes]`, documented and pinned by a known-tiny-composite unit test." (chainspot:.task/CHSPT-82.md:270-271). No DuckDB, no named alternative backend, and no "cold-start budget" language of any kind appears anywhere in this tip's added or changed markdown (grepped `docs/`, `experiments/`, `scripts/chainspot-lab/`, `.task/`, `packages/**/README*` for "duckdb" with zero hits) — recording as missing, matching pyto's own {?} WarmupBudget framing that DuckDB was tried and archived elsewhere, not here.

The RATCHETS.md law encodes a storage/measurement-trust discipline that touches receipts directly: "**STEP 0, before anything else: verify the measurement itself**, per the `receipt-reconcile` skill, BEFORE treating a broken threshold as a footgun firing... A case whose measurement fails either check is a **MEASUREMENT DEFECT**: fix the measuring, leave the threshold untouched." (chainspot:docs/RATCHETS.md:9-16) — a rule that receipts (stored evidence) outrank the reader's threshold assumptions, reusable as a governance pattern for pyto's own retained records.

(chainspot:experiments/parts-inspector/README.md:18-19) — a real PCR execution counted per Tick and per Calculation, exactly pyto's `PrincipleComponentRender -> Tick[]`, `Tick -> Calculation[]` shape (pyto/research/origin.md:20-23), running against ChainSpot's own algorithm rather than pyto's Python core.

(chainspot:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/feature-discovery/REVIEW.md:21) — i.e. a discovery/inspection PCR is allowed to eagerly compute everything (unlike a production path), a distinction pyto's Tick materializer gap (tick-observability-ledger.md section 3) does not yet draw between an inspection run and a production run.
