Earlier writes in the failed fork remain available; partial Calculation records are not yet returned." (chainspot:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md:13).

(chainspot:docs/handoffs/BADGE-PCR-DISCOVERY-SCRIPT.md:13,25) — a PCR's Tick order should mirror the real execution order closely enough that bugs surface as a byproduct of watching it, which is the origin.md founding need restated as a construction rule for the PCR author, not just the viewer.
receipts_and_telemetry:
This tip's receipts are still line-oriented text/JSON files, not a joined Tick-keyed structure — matching the exact gap tick-observability-ledger.md section 3 describes for pyto. docs/RATCHETS.md shows the concrete shape: a run writes `run.receipt.txt` with named `measurement <field> <value>` lines that a threshold-governance process reads back: "Receipt: `artifacts/sweep/dev72-recovered-default/HeritagePark-full/run.receipt.txt`, `measurement padClaimDistancePx` (max=128.99) / `measurement padClaimMedianPx` (64.309) lines" (chainspot:docs/RATCHETS.md:59). scripts/chainspot-lab/README.md documents the Sweep batch receipt shape precisely, including provenance-of-provenance: "Each case writes normal Sweep evidence below `artifacts/sweep/<config>/batches/<course>/<case>/`; the batch root receives compact `summary.txt` and machine-readable `summary.json` receipts... Provenance appears in both receipts: badge/basket counts are accepted drawables from their named trace units... conformance drift counts receipts whose actual consumes/produces omit a declared slot." (chainspot:scripts/chainspot-lab/README.md:232) — "conformance drift" here is exactly pyto's `declared_consumes` vs `actual_consumes` divergence (pyto/research/tick-observability-ledger.md row 27), independently arrived at in ChainSpot's own Sweep receipts.

docs/abfeature-contract.md defines the telemetry primitives a Calculation-equivalent ("unit") must call, which is the clearest reusable API shape in this tip: "**No silent drops**: if your code examines-and-rejects candidates, emit a rejected drawable with a `reason` per kill (`ctx.overlay(id, { type, …, verdict: 'rejected', reason })`). This is the debuggability contract — 'why 0 tees' must be answerable from the raster." (chainspot:docs/abfeature-contract.md:63-66) and "Instrument what you measure: `ctx.measure(id, name, value)` (exact aggregates), `ctx.overlay(...)` (points/boxes/polylines in ORIGINAL-image px), `ctx.heatmap(id, key, float32)` for fields." (chainspot:docs/abfeature-contract.md:67-69). This `measure`/`overlay`/`heatmap` triad is a telemetry vocabulary pyto's Calculation authors could adopt almost verbatim for what a Part's "value" materializes into.

docs/unported/engine-dev72-lineage.md documents the origin of the "no silent drops" rule as a direct response to a real failure ("the trophy-basket disaster"): "A tee candidate that failed a geometry window left no trace at all. The T3 comment in `measure.ts` states the goal exactly: 'no silent drops: every examined-and-killed candidate leaves a rejected drawable with its reason — this is the "why 0 tees?" answer on the raster.'" (chainspot:docs/unported/engine-dev72-lineage.md:92-96) — receipts exist specifically to make negative outcomes (rejections), not just positive ones, inspectable; pyto's `origin.md` names the same failure mode generically ("agents then produced dumb receipts and self-verified," pyto/research/origin.md:14-15) but does not yet have this rejection-with-reason convention anywhere in `pyto/src/pyto/`.
reusable_now: Port `ctx.measure(id, name, value)` / `ctx.overlay(id, {..., verdict, reason})` / `ctx.heatmap(id, key, float32)` (chainspot:docs/abfeature-contract.md:63-69) as pyto's Calculation-side telemetry vocabulary, with the 'no silent drops: every rejected candidate emits a reason' rule as a hard convention for every pyto Calculation that filters or rejects (chainspot:docs/unported/engine-dev72-lineage.md:92-96).

Adopt the content-addressed imageId formula verbatim as pyto's first specialized raster backend key: `sha256([u32be width][u32be height][raw RGBA bytes])` (chainspot:.task/CHSPT-82.md:270-271) — directly answers Reframing 4's 'content addressing as the document identity' for image-kind Parts.

Before building the pyto Day-3 tick-viewer, freeze the receipt JSON shape against a real `PCR.run(observe=True)` output and generate its test fixture from that real run rather than hand-authoring one — this is the explicit lesson of the T5 receipt-viewer failure: 'Reconcile the receipt work shape before writing a viewer. addressing:
No explicit "root", "mount", or "the point is connection" statement exists anywhere in this tip -- that framing is a later, pyto-side/owner concept and is absent here. Report as missing rather than inferred. What the tip does have is a working, disciplined dotted address space:

- SlotRef is kept a plain open string on purpose so finer-grained decomposition never requires a schema change: contract.ts:16-25 -- "Deliberately a plain string, not a closed enum: R2 requires operations at a finer grain than the existing engine units, so the slot namespace has to stay open (e.g. 'badgeStage.brightMask', 'badgeStage.components', 'assignment.scoring', 'assignment.selection') without this file growing every time a unit gets decomposed further." Legality (who-produces-before-who-consumes) is enforced by the compiler's dependency walk, never by the type system (contract.ts:22-24).
- Calculation identities are constrained to a `fn.` prefix at the type level: PxFn.address is typed `` `fn.${string}` `` (board.ts:18), and PQL enforces it at parse time -- pql.ts:60: "if (!call.startsWith('fn.')) throw new Error(`PQL ${where}.call: expected a registered fn. address.`)".
- Part/value addresses observed in receipts and the parts-inspector use a dotted domain.stage.component convention, not a generic root: `px.course.canonicalPixels` (+page.svelte:26), `px.image.cropped` / `px.components.masks` / `px.components` (componentPxC.ts:12-15), and `px.s1.exp.maskComponents.part.blackComponent-115` (receipt.json candidates row) -- each segment names a real domain object, never a placeholder.
- A run itself gets addressed under a `px.pql.` prefix keyed by the composition's own declared name: pql.ts:108 -- `pxc.set(\`px.pql.${composition.PrincipleComponentRender}\`, run);` -- i.e. the "namespace root" that exists in this tip is `px.pql.<name>` for run records specifically, chosen by the PCR's own title rather than assigned generically.
- PxC itself is described as "PxC's browser-safe address space" (board.ts:37-41), with `fork()` for isolated snapshots and `register`/`call` keeping calculation identity distinct from Part storage (board.ts:42-50).

No mounts, no per-namespace backend selection, and no discussion of what makes a root "meaningful" appear in this tip; the owner's later "connection" framing is not represented here at all.
viewer_and_pcr_render:
This tip contains a working, rendering answer to "PCRs are Kibana" that predates the phrase. Two surfaces:

1. `TickInspection.svelte` (src/lib/evidence-workbench/TickInspection.svelte), a Storybook-facing per-Tick panel. Per Tick it renders: an identity strip of "Run Args identity" (`pcr.paramsHash`), "Plan" (`pcr.planFingerprint`), "Run result" (`pcr.runResultId`) plus the honesty line `{pcr.runResultIdentityScope} -- {pcr.runResultIdentityLimitation}` (TickInspection.svelte:40-56); a three-column flow of "Exact PxC inputs" (`tick.actualConsumes`, flagging any declared-but-unread address), "Calculation identity" (`tick.frozenCalculations`, each showing `calculation.address`, its SHA-256 `implementationHash`, its `identityScope`, and the explicit non-transitivity warning `calculation.limitation`), and "Exact PxC outputs" (`tick.writes`, each address plus its `kind`, with `replacement` writes visually flagged) (TickInspection.svelte:58-97); a "Materializations emitted by this Tick" section listing each artifact's kind/id/sha256/dims, or else the explicit line "No persisted Materialization at this boundary. PxC outputs remain inspectable by address." when none exist (TickInspection.svelte:100-119); and a "Residue / UNKNOWN" section that is either populated with named unexplained-pixel counts or shows "UNKNOWN -- this Tick establishes no molecule-specific residue account." (TickInspection.svelte:122-133).

2. `PcrInspectionHost.svelte` composes several PCRs/specimens over that per-Tick panel and computes a `renderId` via `pcrRenderId(pcr, {materializationView, zoom, showGrid, showReceipt, specimenId})` (PcrInspectionHost.svelte:72-76), with the header note "Projection-only MaterializationView -- View Args never cross the production gateway" (PcrInspectionHost.svelte:107-109). `pcr.ts:90-93` defines that function with the comment "View identity is a pure projection of a frozen PCR; it cannot execute CV." `pcr.ts:18-21` states the governing rule directly: "Storybook-facing composition of already-executed Tick testimony. PCR has deliberately no run() method: the production gateway is the only execution authority and hands this function the receipts it already produced."

A second, separate viewer is the DuckDB experiment's own `/parts` page (src/staging-routes/parts/+page.svelte): it seeds PxC with a saved S0 raster, runs the S1 YAML once, then renders `QueryPanel` (SQL presets over the projected run) beside `PartInspector` (the raw pixel Parts), so a person sees a value (the pixels) fed by a query that selected it -- but this view is keyed by SQL result row / Part identity, not by Tick, and shows no Calculation identity or write-kind at all; it complements TickInspection rather than replacing it.
storage:
DuckDB-Wasm is the backend under test, and the tip is explicit about the boundary it drew and why it failed the budget:

- `projectRun` (src/lib/parts-query/projection.ts:64-144) walks a completed `PqlRun` and produces three scalar-only tables -- `results` (2,163 rows: one per Calculation output item, with tick/call/output_address/collection/label/id/kind/verdict/status/reason), `parts` (1,130 rows: one per distinct component/mask, with id/kind/pixel_count/bbox/polarity/label/bbox_source_result), and `result_parts` (2,390 rows: result-to-part occurrence with a `role_path`). The doc comment states the boundary: "Project a completed PQL run into scalar DuckDB tables. Pixel buffers stay in PxC and are only measured." (projection.ts:63).
- `tables.ts` loads these into DuckDB inside one transaction with escaped SQL literals and batched 200-row inserts (tables.ts:12-35); `database.ts` opens one disposable in-memory DuckDB-Wasm instance per completed run via `openRunDatabase`, with the comment "One disposable database per completed run. PxC remains the source of the actual Parts." (database.ts:9).
- Content addressing is present at two layers: `FrozenCalculation.implementationHash` is "SHA-256 of the bound executable function body in this runtime build" with an honest scope tag `identityScope: 'runtime-function-body'` and limitation "called helpers, constants, templates, and assets are not covered" (contract.ts:60-68); and `ArtifactRef` is a "Content-addressed reference to an artifact the sink has stored" carrying `sha256`, a sink-defined opaque `uri`, and optional `dims` (contract.ts:90-113). The DuckDB experiment's own receipt.json records `sourceRgbaSha256` and `compositionSha256` for the exact run it queried.
- What was archived and why, verbatim from REPORT.md: "One final Node run measured S1 at 613 ms, projection at 46 ms, and database initialization plus table loading at 3.80 s... The browser preview measured startup at 5.79 s... The exception-handling Wasm asset is 34,242,586 bytes uncompressed... DuckDB adds substantial startup weight for this small dataset. No CV speedup was attempted or demonstrated." The report's own responsibility boundary: "PxC and PQL retain execution and original material. No core store, registry, executor, or YAML edits were required... Projection reads a completed run. SQL holds scalar records and identity links; raw pixel buffers stay with the Parts... DuckDB owns relational query execution... This is deliberately a single completed-run query surface. It does not provide live subscriptions, cross-run versioning, a general SQL editor, arbitrary PxC enumeration, or execution optimization."
- No StorageKinds-style "backend chosen by address prefix" exists in this tip; DuckDB was evaluated as a single global projection layer over one run, not as a namespace-scoped backend, and it was rejected outright rather than scoped down.
materialization_and_ticks:
`materialize` is one of exactly five allowed OperationKind verbs: "'measure' | 'transform' | 'compute' | 'decide' | 'materialize'" (contract.ts:13). A `Materialization` is formally an `ArtifactRef` -- id, kind, sha256, uri, optional dims (contract.ts:90-113) -- handed to an injected sink; the exec core "imports nothing and reaches no I/O" (contract.ts:1-10), so materializing is deliberately kept outside the pure execution core.

The most load-bearing finding for pyto's `{?} CacheInvalidation` is `Pcr`'s own stated identity limitation: `runResultIdentityScope: 'tick-testimony-and-materializations'` and `runResultIdentityLimitation: 'opaque PxC output values require an emitted Materialization'` (pcr.ts:29-31). In other words: a PCR's content-addressed `runResultId` is a hash over Tick testimony only (pcr.ts:70-76); an opaque PxC value that was never explicitly materialized is NOT covered by that identity at all. `TickInspection.svelte` makes this gap visible to a person rather than hiding it: when `tick.artifacts` is empty it prints "No persisted Materialization at this boundary. PxC outputs remain inspectable by address." (TickInspection.svelte:115-119) -- i.e. the UI names the exact condition under which run identity does not reach a value.

`materializeBadgeSpecimens.mjs` (src/lib/server/evidence-workbench/materializeBadgeSpecimens.mjs) is the Node-side materializer that actually runs a real detector pipeline (`compileExecutionPlan` -> `executeCompiledPlan` -> `composePcr`) against a real or corpus image and decodes each artifact kind into Storybook-ready fixtures, falling back to an explicit "unavailable" specimen (with the note "Real E materialization unavailable: ... does not exist. Set CHAINSPOT_BADGE_IMAGE or place chainspot-corpus beside ChainSpot.") when no real input exists (materializeBadgeSpecimens.mjs:37-51) -- a concrete pattern for "declare the gap rather than fabricate a value" that pyto's own generate_returns.py citation-or-fail rule already mirrors independently.

receipts_and_telemetry:
The `Receipt` shape (== `TickTestimony`, contract.ts:127-148) is: `opId`, `frozenCalculations: FrozenCalculation[]`, `startedAtMs`, `durationMs`, `declaredConsumes`/`declaredProduces`, `actualConsumes`/`actualProduces`, `writes: PxWriteTestimony[]`, `probes: Probe[]`, `artifacts: ArtifactRef[]`. Two fields are more granular than anything documented yet in pyto:

- `PxWriteTestimony` is `{address, kind: 'new-address' | 'refinement' | 'replacement'}` (contract.ts:71-74), and the doc comment on `Receipt.writes` states the policy directly: "Collision-visible PxC writes; replacements are never hidden as ordinary output." (contract.ts:137). `trackAccess` in board.ts computes this kind live by checking `board.has(slot)` and whether the address was in the Tick's own `declaredConsumes` before the write (board.ts:119-131) -- a three-way richer signal than pyto's current binary "hit" (`{?} HitDefinition`).
- `Probe` is a tiny named-telemetry primitive distinct from writes or artifacts: `{name: string, value: number}` (contract.ts:115-119), described as "A single named numeric observation captured during an operation's run" -- exactly the kind of cheap scalar telemetry pyto's Receipt today has no field for at all (`tick-observability-ledger.md` section 3, item 3: "Receipt has no value field").
- `accessConformance?: 'exact'` (contract.ts:51) is an opt-in strict mode a `Tick`/OperationSpec can declare; `gateway.ts:117` throws "PxC: Tick '...' access contradicts its declaration; ..." when actual and declared consumes/produces diverge under that mode -- a stricter, characterized answer to pyto's open `{?} SilentRules` (whether pcr.py should raise at declaration time).
- The actual DuckDB experiment's `receipt.json` (both the duckdb-inspection and parts-inspector variants) shows the concrete telemetry shape in practice: `sourceCommit`, `sourceImage`, `sourceRgbaSha256`, `compositionSha256`, `engine`, `engineRuntime`, `executionMs`/`projectionMs`/`databaseMs`, `ticks`, `calculations`, `tables: {results, parts, result_parts}`, `candidates`, `incomplete`, `selectedPlates`, `rejectedPlates`, `queries: [{id, title, sql, elapsedMs, rows}]`, `selectedCandidate`, `selectedTarget`, `selectedParts`, `checks`, `browserVerified` -- durations and digests sit beside literal row data in one file, unlike pyto's current split across `testimony.json`/`receipts.json`/`retained.json`.
- A telemetry-discipline warning surfaces twice in `docs/unported/g3-intact-tee-family.md` (lines 108 and 244): a diagnostic-only scalar (`grayCount`) that was only ever `console.log`'d must never become a decision input -- "LAB gray payload (145 <= max(R,G,B) <= 175) was DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. It never selected/rejected this family. Do not add a gray kill rule." This is a live, named case of the exact discipline pyto's `probes`/`Observation` split should preserve: cheap named numbers are for people to read, never for a Calculation to branch on silently.

commit_message: Checkpoint S1 YAML composition, calculation variants, and JS inspection
what_it_is: A ~1258-file checkpoint (155k insertions / 140k deletions vs main b1f4c83) that lands, for the first time in the clone, a real `packages/alg/src/exec/**` PxC/PCR/PQL/Tick execution kernel in TypeScript, wires it into S0-S3 Stage contracts and an experimental S1 badge-assembly composition declared in a `PrincipleComponentRender.yaml`, and ships a dependency-free browser HTML inspector (`renderPqlHtml`) that reads a PQL run and lets a person click through Ticks/Calculations/Parts. It is the ChainSpot-side, already-running version of exactly the vocabulary pyto's origin.md and ULTRACODE-WEEK.md Reframing 4 describe (PrincipleComponentRender -> Ticks -> Calculations, PCR-as-Kibana, JS as reference semantics) plus the two open pyto questions {?} StorageKinds and {?} Architecture. Most of the diff (docs/, .task/, experiments/dashs-track-edge-sensing/, the seven-whys/orchestration reports) is unrelated CV forensics work bundled into the same checkpoint commit and does not bear on PxC/PCR/addressing.
addressing: Two address families, both plain strings, not closed enums, and both dotted namespaces meant to discriminate. (1) SlotRef / px.* Part addresses: "Deliberately a plain string, not a closed enum: R2 requires operations at a finer grain than the existing engine units, so the slot namespace has to stay open (e.g. 'badgeStage.brightMask', 'badgeStage.components', 'assignment.scoring', 'assignment.selection') without this file growing every time a unit gets decomposed further." (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/contract.ts:15-22). In practice these are dotted hierarchies that read as a path from Stage to sub-part: `px.image.cropped`, `px.components.masks`, `px.components` (5607611:packages/alg/src/stages/componentPxC.ts:12-16), and inside the S1 experiment `px.s1.exp.maskComponents.part.blackMask`, `px.s1.exp.badgeAssembly.plates` etc. (5607611:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/PrincipleComponentRender.yaml:7,12,53). (2) fn.* Calculation addresses, same discipline, checked at parse time: "if (!call.startsWith('fn.')) throw new Error(`PQL ${where}.call: expected a registered fn. address.`)" (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/pql.ts:60), giving addresses like `fn.s1.exp.badgeAssembly.selectComponents` (5607611:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/index.ts:110-112). There is no single global "root" segment or generic top-level label anywhere in this address space — every first segment already names a real thing (`px`, `fn`) and every subsequent segment narrows (stage id, `exp`, sub-experiment name, part role), which is the closest concrete precedent in this tip to the owner's "a meaningless root is wasted log(N) potential" rule: nothing here spends a segment on a label that doesn't discriminate. Runs are addressed the same way: the PQL run record itself is written back into the store at `px.pql.<PrincipleComponentRender-id>` — "pxc.set(`px.pql.${composition.PrincipleComponentRender}`, run);" (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/pql.ts:108) — and a Stage's set of variant results at `px.pql.<Stage>.results` (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/stage.ts:43; corroborated in prose at 5607611:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md:12: "The caller receives results and the input PxC stores them at px.pql.<Stage>.results."). "Mount"/"namespace" as pyto's `{?} StorageKinds`/`{?} PerAppBudget` use those words (a backend chosen per address prefix or namespace) is NOT present in this tip: no code here selects a storage backend by address prefix, and grep for "mount" across the diff's exec/stage code returns nothing — the only per-address dispatch implemented is `Part` role (mask/component/scalar) inferred structurally at render time (see viewer section), not a declared storage kind. So this tip advances the *shape* of addresses (open dotted strings, `px.`/`fn.` prefixes, no closed registry) but does not resolve `{?} StorageKinds` or the mounts question at all.
viewer_and_pcr_render: Per-Tick, per-Calculation, with values, not just addresses — this is the ChainSpot-side answer to the pyto tick-observability-ledger's §3 gap ("No function in pyto/src/pyto/ consumes a PcrRun"). `invokePql` executes a `PqlComposition` (Ticks -> Calculations, each `call`/`with`/`args`/`into`) synchronously in declaration order and records, per Calculation, `actualCall`, resolved `inputs`, `args`, and `output` "held by reference rather than copied" (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/pql.ts:14-31,83-109 — comment at line 20-22). `renderPqlHtml` turns that `PqlRun` into a self-contained, dependency-free HTML page: "A portable inspector over actual Calculation outputs, with no detector calls." (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/render.ts:25). It builds a per-operation dropdown (`${c.tick} / ${c.call}`), a details pane dumping `{tick, call, args, into}` as JSON, and a pixel-layer SVG view via `pixelLayers()`, which walks the output value structurally and dispatches on a `.kind` tag: `if(node.kind==='cropped-raster')return;` / `if(node.kind==='component'||node.kind==='mask'){...}` (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/render.ts:67-71) — i.e., Part *kind* is inferred from the value's own tag at render time, not declared on the address (contrast with pyto's `{?}` gap #4 in tick-observability-ledger.md: "No way to tell an image Part from a scalar Part... There is no kind, dtype, or renderer tag"). `renderPartsSvg` composites one `<path>` per pixel layer with run-length-encoded rows into one SVG, with an "Export current SVG" button. The REVIEW.md is explicit that this is descriptive and not a scoring tool: "View controls perform no CV calculations." (5607611:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md:14). PCR itself (`composePcr` in pcr.ts) is a separate, narrower artifact: a frozen, content-hashed *identity* over already-executed Tick testimony for Storybook, explicitly refusing to be an execution surface — "PCR has deliberately no run() method: the production gateway is the only execution authority and hands this function the receipts it already produced." (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/pcr.ts:17-20). It computes `runResultId = sha256(planFingerprint, paramsHash, frozenTickIdentity(tick)[])` and separately `pcrRenderId(pcr, viewArgs)` as "a pure projection of a frozen PCR; it cannot execute CV" (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/pcr.ts:90-92). It self-declares the scope limit pyto also hit: "Explicitly bounded: opaque PxC values are not silently claimed as content-frozen." / `runResultIdentityLimitation: 'opaque PxC output values require an emitted Materialization'` (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/pcr.ts:29-31) — the same value-vs-digest gap tick-observability-ledger.md documents for pyto's `Receipt.result_sha256`.
storage: No DuckDB and no specialized-backend-by-prefix code anywhere in this tip (grep across the diff for "duckdb" is empty); the storage story here is entirely in-memory PxC plus one concrete content-addressing precedent. PxC ("PxC's browser-safe address space") is a plain in-memory Map-backed store: `export function createExecBoard(): PxC { return boardFrom(new Map(), new Map()); }` (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/board.ts:52,54), with `get`/`has`/`set`/`register`/`call` and a `fork()` that "snapshots slot and function maps... shares immutable values, including raster buffers. Each run's writes stay in its own fork." (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/board.ts:44 comment; corroborated in prose at 5607611:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/exp/badge-assembly/REVIEW.md:11). This is the ABFeature-tournament mechanism: `createPqlStage` forks PxC once per variant (Default + each registered feature), runs the same composition against each fork with calculation overrides, and keeps every fork's failed and successful writes (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/stage.ts:25-41; REVIEW.md:13 "Variant failures produce failed results and do not suppress later variants. Earlier writes in the failed fork remain available"). Content addressing exists as a real, shipped convention one layer up (G0 intake, not PxC itself): "canonical composite materialization: real pixel flattening (Node-runnable, no canvas) + content-addressed `imageId` = sha256 over `[u32be widthPx][u32be heightPx][raw RGBA bytes]`, documented and pinned by a known-tiny-composite unit test." (5607611:.task/CHSPT-82.md:269-272). Artifacts extracted during a Tick run are also content-addressed at the sink boundary: `ArtifactRef` carries `sha256` and a sink-defined `uri`, "a file:// path from the Node sink, an in-memory handle from a browser/collector sink) — the exec core never interprets it, only carries it through the receipt." (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/contract.ts:90-108, comment at 90-95). Nothing in this tip answers pyto's `{?} StorageKinds` (backend chosen by address prefix or declared Part kind) — there is exactly one backend (the in-memory Map board) and one content-addressing convention (image sha256), not a facade over several.
materialization_and_ticks: "Materialize" is used with a specific, disciplined meaning: a materialization is PCR-only render output, never written back to PxC as a Part. S1's contract explicitly states the rule in its own receipt text: `'materialization: subtraction rasters are PCR output only; they are not written to PxC'` (5607611:packages/alg/src/stages/S1/contract.ts:24), produced by `materializeS1Subtractions(run)` (same file, line 9) which derives display rasters (BadgePx subtraction, Badge mute subtraction panels) from the already-computed `run` without mutating the PxC the run returned. Tick-as-synchronization-boundary is enforced structurally, not just documented: `executeCompiledPlan` walks `plan.ops` in order, wraps the board once per operation with `trackAccess` (recording `consumed`/`produced`/`writes` for exactly that op), runs the implementation, times it (`durationMs = now() - startedAtMs`), and only then asserts `assertAccessConformance` when `op.accessConformance === 'exact'`, throwing on any declared/actual read or write mismatch — "PxC: Tick '${op.id}' access contradicts its declaration; missing reads=[...] extra reads=[...] missing writes=[...] extra writes=[...]." (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/gateway.ts:103-122, throw text at 116-120). `trackAccess` is the mechanism, wrapping (not replacing) the board: "Wraps a board so every get()/set() call made through the wrapper during one operation's run is recorded — the gateway's source for `actualConsumes`/`actualProduces` on that operation's Receipt." (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/board.ts:82-86). A synchronous and an async gateway variant exist (`executeCompiledPlan` / `executeCompiledPlanAsync`), both producing the identical `Receipt` shape, which is exactly the "JS as reference semantics, node vs browser" split pyto's Reframing 4 calls for.

It is not a transitive source or dependency hash." line 65-67), `startedAtMs`/`durationMs`, `declaredConsumes`/`declaredProduces` vs `actualConsumes`/`actualProduces`, `writes: readonly PxWriteTestimony[]` where each write is classified `'new-address' | 'refinement' | 'replacement'` based on whether the address existed before and whether it was declared as consumed — "Collision-visible PxC writes; replacements are never hidden as ordinary output." (line 137, classification logic at 5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/board.ts:119-131), `probes: readonly Probe[]` (generic `{name, value}` shape-probes: "for every slot an operation actually produced, record its element count when the value is array-like" — 5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/gateway.ts:83-101), and `artifacts: readonly ArtifactRef[]` (`{id, kind, sha256, uri, dims?}`). `TickTestimony` is literally `type TickTestimony = Receipt` (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/contract.ts:148), i.e. this tip's Tick and Receipt are the same object — there is no separate testimony-vs-receipt split the way pyto's `TickTestimony`/`Receipt` are two structures joined by invocation id; pyto's tick-observability-ledger.md's "No Tick↔receipt join" gap (§3 item 2) does not exist in this ChainSpot design because there was never a second object to join. `PCR.frozenTickIdentity` strips a tick's testimony down to `{opId, frozenCalculations, actualConsumes, actualProduces, writes, artifacts}` (dims and value-bearing fields explicitly excluded) before hashing it into `runResultId` (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/pcr.ts:35-49) — the digest is over structure/identity, never over opaque Part values, matching pyto's `Receipt.result_sha256` boundary. `ABFeatureSetManifest` layers a set-level telemetry record on top of per-op Receipts: `manifestHash` is computed over a `semanticReceipt` that deliberately excludes wall-clock fields — "Deterministic semantic receipt hash; wall-clock fields are intentionally excluded." (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/feature-set.ts:113, exclusion at 345-349: `operations.map(({startedAtMs, durationMs, ...receipt}) => {void startedAtMs; void durationMs; return receipt;})`) — a concrete instance of separating a byte-stable identity channel from a timing/telemetry channel, which is exactly pyto's own `{?} ObservationSeam` design (digests/durations off to the side so consumer bytes stay stable). `formatABFeatureSetManifestMarkdown` (5607611:packages/alg/src/exec/feature-set.ts:367-409) is a plain-text/markdown receipt report per operation (time, declared/actual consumes/produces, probes, artifacts) — the nearest thing in this tip to pyto's `comparison.md`.

commit_message: feat(alg): preserve composed open-frame Tee recovery and six-course findings (Samuel Mahan, Sat Sep 5 07:49:10 2026 -0500). git diff --stat main 5433854: 1144 files changed, 110604 insertions(+), 139825 deletions(-) -- a near-total tree rewrite/rebase, not an incremental change. The requested subset (docs/, experiments/**, scripts/chainspot-lab/**, packages/**/README*, .task/**) alone is 162 files, +32322/-4603.
what_it_is: Despite the title, this tip is not primarily a Tee-recovery result -- it is the commit where ChainSpot's execution kernel (PxC / Tick / PCR / receipts, an ELK-shaped store-plus-compose-plus-view architecture) and its LAB tool (scripts/chainspot-lab) were formalized in committed code and docs, alongside in-flight six-course Stage S0-S4 Tee detection/recovery experiments (docs/lab/arc-stage-seams/*, packages/alg/src/stages/S4/exp/**). It is effectively the JS reference-semantics twin of what pyto's ULTRACODE-WEEK plan wants built in Python: a working PxC store (packages/alg/src/exec/board.ts), a Receipt/Tick contract (contract.ts), a content-addressed PCR composition (pcr.ts), an injected-sink storage boundary with a Node filesystem sink and a browser-safe in-memory sink (sink.ts, node-sink.ts), and a Storybook-based per-Tick viewer that renders exactly what pyto's tick-observability-ledger says pyto itself lacks (src/lib/evidence-workbench/{PcrInspectionHost,TickInspection}.svelte). No PQL, no DuckDB, and no explicit "mount"/namespace-per-backend model appear anywhere in this tip -- those are pyto-side (or later ChainSpot-branch) concepts not yet present here.
addressing: Root/prefix rule: addresses are plain strings under an open namespace, deliberately not a closed enum -- contract.ts:16-24 says the "slot namespace has to stay open ... without this file growing every time a unit gets decomposed further," with "Legality of who-produces-before-who-consumes ... enforced by the compiler's dependency walk, not by the type system." In practice every address is `px.<domain>.<field>` (board.ts's `pxKey`/`PxKey<T>` wraps a `SlotRef`, contract.ts:25 `export type SlotRef = string`), and the domain segment is chosen to carry meaning rather than being generic: S0/clean/index.ts:15-17 defines `px.source.selectedInput`, `px.source.fullImage`, and -- for the same crop step's OUTPUT -- `px.course.canonicalPixels`, deliberately switching the root from `source` to `course` at the moment the pixels become the task's canonical subject (S0/clean/index.ts:31-41's `S0_CROP_TICK` note: "Crop the decoded FullImage and materialize the CroppedImage in PxC"). That is a concrete instance of the owner's "root must discriminate, not label" rule, done in the wild rather than stated as a rule. Calculation addresses are `fn.*` (contract.ts:49, board.ts's `PxFn`/`pxFn`). No mount/backend-per-namespace model or explicit written addressing RULE document was found in this tip -- the discipline is enforced structurally (compiler dependency walk, `accessConformance: 'exact'` on OperationSpec, contract.ts:51) rather than declared in prose. \"Connection\" as the owner frames it shows up as PxC's own wording: WORLD_BOOT.md:33-34 -- \"PxC -- the presently materialized computational world. Values have semantic addresses such as px.*; calculations have identities such as fn.*.\" / \"Tick -- one declared transition that reads PxC addresses, delegates to real computation, and writes PxC addresses.\" Pages (scratch/notes/final search overlays) are explicitly named as address-space namespaces, not raster copies: scripts/chainspot-lab/README.md:185 -- \"Pages are visibility/mutation namespaces, not raster copies.\" LAB course/context addressing is likewise explicit data, never filename heuristics: README.md:97 -- \"Known course manifests live under `scripts/chainspot-lab/courses/` ... They are explicit data, not hidden filename heuristics.\"
viewer_and_pcr_render: The viewer is a real, working per-Tick Storybook surface, not a proposal. Glossary (scripts/chainspot-lab/WORLD_BOOT.md:35, 37-38): \"PCR -- an ordered record of meaningful Ticks and their state. A PCR does not schedule or execute work.\" / \"Story -- an actual Storybook Story that composes Molecules to render a PCR. Storybook is the rendering and interaction-test mechanism.\" The concrete render, per Tick, lives in TickInspection.svelte: a header with the PCR title and Tick opId plus durationMs (line ~37); an identity strip of `pcr.paramsHash`, `pcr.planFingerprint`, `pcr.runResultId` (TickInspection.svelte:41-53) with the honesty caveat printed inline at line 55 -- `{pcr.runResultIdentityScope} -- {pcr.runResultIdentityLimitation}`; three columns -- \"Exact PxC inputs\" (line 60, `tick.actualConsumes`, plus a warning for declared-but-unread), \"Calculation identity\" (line 71, each `fn.*` address with its SHA-256 implementation hash and an explicit \"Not transitive\" limitation string), \"Exact PxC outputs\" (line 84, `tick.writes` with write kind, flagging `replacement`); a \"Materializations emitted by this Tick\" section (line 101) listing each artifact's kind, id, SHA-256, and dims when known; and a \"Residue / UNKNOWN\" section (line 123) that is per-molecule and explicitly allowed to say UNKNOWN rather than fabricate a number. PcrInspectionHost.svelte wraps this with a hard separation between what the production gateway computed and what is pure projection: its header literally reads \"Projection-only MaterializationView\" / \"View Args never cross the production gateway\" (PcrInspectionHost.svelte:90-93), and computes a `renderId` via `pcrRenderId(pcr, {materializationView, zoom, showGrid, showReceipt, specimenId})` (line 79) -- i.e. the render's own identity is a hash of (frozen run result, view args), matching pcr.ts's `pcrRenderId` doc: \"View identity is a pure projection of a frozen PCR; it cannot execute CV\" (pcr.ts:90). What a person sees is per-Tick structure (inputs/calc/outputs/materializations/residue), not raw per-Calculation values inline -- values are reached only through emitted Materializations (artifact refs) or through a molecule-specific projection component (`BadgeEvidenceView`, `M1EvidenceView`) selected by `pcr.id`, so PxC values that never got materialized stay opaque by design (pcr.ts:29-31: \"Explicitly bounded: opaque PxC values are not silently claimed as content-frozen\" / \"opaque PxC output values require an emitted Materialization\"). This is driven by real Storybook Stories per checkpoint (PcrInspection.stories.ts:55-98, e.g. `BadgeMasks`, `TeeRecovery`) and by a staging route: src/lib/evidence-workbench/README.md:27-30 -- \"`/lab/pcr` reuses the Storybook inspection molecules against the same materialized computation. It opens with the checked `DEFAULT_PCR_INSPECTION_PLAN` ... The staging build fails loudly if the corpus is absent or any default PCR, Tick, or specimen identity has drifted.\"
storage: No DuckDB anywhere in this tip (0 grep hits for "duckdb" across the whole extracted tree). Storage is an injected-sink boundary, deliberately kept out of the browser-safe core: sink.ts:1-8 -- \"the injected sink boundary. executeCompiledPlan (gateway.ts) never touches disk itself -- it hands artifact bytes and receipts to whatever ExecSink the caller provides ... The Node filesystem sink lives in node-sink.ts, a separate module the core never imports.\" Two concrete backends ship: `createMemorySink()` (sink.ts:28-54), the \"browser-safe default,\" storing artifacts in a `Map<string, Uint8Array>` keyed by the caller-given id, with a `memory://<id>` URI and a SHA-256 computed via `sha256HexSync(bytes)` per artifact -- content is verified/addressed by digest but located by caller-chosen id, not by the digest itself; and `createNodeSink(outDir)` (node-sink.ts:1-36), which writes `<outDir>/artifacts/<kind>/<id>.bin` and appends one JSON `Receipt` per line to `<outDir>/receipts.jsonl` (node-sink.ts:4-9, 17-35) -- kind-sharded directories, id-named files, digest carried as a field on the `ArtifactRef` rather than as the filename. A no-op `createNullSink()` (sink.ts:18-26) exists for the trace-off fast path (hashes/stores nothing). `ArtifactRef` itself (contract.ts:104-113) is `{id, kind, sha256, uri, dims?}` -- `uri` is explicitly sink-defined and opaque to the exec core (contract.ts:90-95: \"the exec core never interprets it, only carries it through the receipt\"). No warm-start cost data (pyto's 5000ms-budget concern) appears in this tip for either sink; per pyto's WarmupBudget resolution, only a backend that is measured against a per-namespace budget counts as a runtime backend versus a workshop-only one, and no such measurement exists here for node-sink. Separately, ChainSpot's Sweep batch runner writes non-kernel evidence under `artifacts/sweep/<config>/batches/<course>/<case>/` with `summary.txt`/`summary.json` (scripts/chainspot-lab/README.md:230-232) -- a second, older receipt convention that predates/parallels the PxC ExecSink one and is not itself content-addressed.
materialization_and_ticks: Glossary: WORLD_BOOT.md:36 -- \"Materialization -- an already-computed PxC value made drawable or otherwise inspectable. It is not a second source of truth.\" A Tick is `contract.ts`'s `Receipt` read as testimony (contract.ts:143-148: \"A Tick is the existing gateway Receipt understood as inspection testimony: exact addresses in, frozen calculations, exact addresses out. It adds no execution authority and deliberately has no run() method.\"). `PxC.set`/`.get` are wrapped per-Tick by `trackAccess` (board.ts:80-134), which records `actualConsumes`/`actualProduces`/`writes` (each write classified `new-address | refinement | replacement`, board.ts:120-127) independent of what the OperationSpec merely `declares` -- a direct, working analogue of pyto's declared-vs-actual divergence design. Calculation identity is frozen per Tick via `gateway.ts`'s `freezeCalculations` (gateway.ts:57-81): SHA-256 of `Function.prototype.toString.call(binding.calculate)` (line 77), i.e. the function's own source text, matching pyto's `implementation_sha256` notion but computed differently (source-text hash, not a bytecode/object hash), and explicitly scoped as \"runtime-function-body\" with \"called helpers, constants, templates, and assets are not covered\" (contract.ts:65-68). A PCR is a frozen, content-addressed composition of already-run Ticks, never itself an executor: pcr.ts:17-21 -- \"Storybook-facing composition of already-executed Tick testimony. PCR has deliberately no run() method: the production gateway is the only execution authority and hands this function the receipts it already produced.\" Its `runResultId` is `sha256(canonicalJson({planFingerprint, paramsHash, ticks: frozenTickIdentity(...)}))` (pcr.ts:35-49, 70-76) -- content addressing as the PCR's own identity, matching pyto's ELK "content addressing as the document identity" framing (ULTRACODE-WEEK.md Reframing 4). There is no single generic Tick materializer dispatched by Part/value kind the way pyto's tick-observability-ledger says pyto lacks (section 3): dispatch is per-operation-id via `ARTIFACT_EXTRACTORS: Readonly<Record<string, (board) => OperationArtifact[]>>` (gateway.ts:19, 42-44) -- i.e. ChainSpot has the same gap pyto has, solved the same way pyto's problem #4 describes as missing (\"no kind/dtype/renderer tag ... dispatch is hardcoded per stage\"), just with a registry keyed by opId instead of by Stage. Generic, kind-independent instrumentation does exist at the operation level: `shapeProbes` (gateway.ts:83-100) auto-records `{slot}.length` for every produced array-like value with no per-Tick author effort, an ROI-cheap idea pyto does not yet have.
receipts_and_telemetry: The `Receipt` type (contract.ts:127-141) is the canonical shape: `{opId, frozenCalculations: FrozenCalculation[], startedAtMs, durationMs, declaredConsumes, declaredProduces, actualConsumes, actualProduces, writes: PxWriteTestimony[], probes: Probe[], artifacts: ArtifactRef[]}`, with the doc comment (contract.ts:121-126): \"`declared*` comes from the OperationSpec; `actual*` comes from what the operation really touched on the evidence board while running. The two diverging is a conformance failure the gateway surfaces rather than silently accepting.\" `Probe` (contract.ts:115-119) is `{name, value: number}` -- a flat named-metric shape, simpler than pyto's testimony but directly comparable to pyto's Calculation-level measurements. `FrozenCalculation` (contract.ts:60-68) is `{address: fn.*, implementationHash, identityScope: 'runtime-function-body', limitation}`. `PxWriteTestimony` (contract.ts:71-74) is `{address, kind: 'new-address'|'refinement'|'replacement'}`. Separately, an older/parallel telemetry convention survives from the pre-PxC engine (docs/INTAKE-ENGINE-HANDOFF.md, dated 2026-08-27, explicitly marked superseded by the operation-DAG/Sweep handoff for the ABFeature contract, docs/abfeature-contract.md:9-11): a run receipt written to `artifacts/sweep/.../run.receipt.{json,txt}` reporting counts and a warning/drift tally -- INTAKE-ENGINE-HANDOFF.md:87 \"Results: 18 badges, 18 baskets, 15 visible tees, 3 recovered tees, 18 total tees, 18 assignments, and 4,860 raw pairs.\" and line 95 \"Receipt warnings: 0; operation conformance drift: 0.\" Sweep's batch aggregate (scripts/chainspot-lab/README.md:230-233) enumerates the ordered fields it writes per case/course: \"course/case/inputs, badges, baskets, raw rings, pre-family tees, visible tees, visible deficit, operation count, runtime, conformance drift, and status,\" explicitly noting \"`durationMs` is volatile by design.\" `ctx.measure`/`ctx.overlay`/`ctx.heatmap` (docs/abfeature-contract.md, \"Instrument what you measure\" section) is the still-older per-feature telemetry API, with an explicit debuggability rule: \"No silent drops: if your code examines-and-rejects candidates, emit a rejected drawable with a `reason` per kill.\" No dedicated PQL query surface or telemetry aggregation layer exists in this tip; "telemetry" as a word appears only in .task/docs warning AGAINST turning a diagnostic-only measurement into a gate (docs/unported/g3-intact-tee-family.md:108: \"LAB gray payload (145 <= max(R,G,B) <= 175) was DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. It never selected or rejected this family. Do not add a gray kill rule.\").
